   From the camp stop inward, beds go by camp and kind (work; life: steps, play, animals; the murmur bed joins in α17); from the valley stop out, each camp is one hum at its members' loudness-weighted centre; only figures drawn in full and loud events play singly (A13.7), and A13.3's steps 2–4 now send a layer's overflow to its beds instead of dropping it.
   A13.7's zoom table (singles, beds and ambience gains by stop, eased between stops) and its rules for speed: marks follow the animation's steady pace while figures are full; at most one event sound per source every 0.5 s and one thunderclap every 2 s; beds follow how many sources there are and how loud, never counting events per game second, gliding over 0.3 s, the weather over 1 s; paused, the ambience holds the moment's weather at −6 dB.

**On the phone:**
1. Install this alpha's APK from the note; Make test world `a16c · Storm over the valley`, then open it from Worlds, with sound on.
2. At the valley stop, hear the wind; pan toward the river and its rush grows.
3. Wait for the storm: rain hisses, a flash, and thunder a few seconds later, rolling longer when far away.
4. Pinch in to close camp, then out again: single taps and footsteps give way to one hum of the camp, which fades as you rise.
5. Turn the camera so the cliff stands between you and the camp: its sounds go dull; pinch in at the cave mouth: sounds inside echo.
6. Run on to dawn with the dial: birds start in the woods; in Settings, the credits list each recording.

**Not in this alpha:** voices, laughs, cries and the murmur bed (α17); the sea and waves, rain on leaves and snow's hush (α20a); wind and leaves shaped by cover, and birdsong everywhere (α21); animals everywhere (α22a); ice's steps and silent frozen water (α20a); the globe's silence (α19b); music (α34a).

**Risks:** too few clearly licensed recordings of the island's animals: the code-made stand-ins are named in the note and the stage report (A13.5); beds sounding like noise: the wash and grains are tuned by ear with the owner at the stage review (α17c, `RSK-28`); the line test costly with many sources: 8 height reads a source, measured within the planner's 0.25 ms.

### α17 The murmur (about 5.5 hours)

**Goal:** people are heard talking in a murmur strung from their language's own sounds, never real words, a child, a woman, a man and an elder each with a voice of their own, muffled and joined in a murmur bed, with laughter, crying, calls and screams; the phone plays the stage's busiest sound scene without a break, and the stage's sound reel is ready for you.

**Tasks:**
1. `T17.1` **The murmur plan and the banned list (`CUL-17`, `SND-03`, A9.2, A9.3).** α06a's `make_language` (`kd-culture/src/lang.rs`) gains A9.3's murmur inputs, the only phrase plan: for a woman's and a man's base voice, 200 phrases each of 2–6 base words (3–14 syllables), tagged statement (50%), question (20%), call (15%), soothing (10%) or sharp (5%), drawn from its own system-11 purpose so a world's words stay as they were; they are kept in the `Language` (`murmur`) in `cul.lang`, and a migration builds them for worlds made earlier from the same draws (A14.9).
   `kd-sim` copies them into A13.9's `MurmurPlan` (in `kd-view`, which `kd-culture` cannot see, A2.2) for `kd-app`'s stringing.
   `data/culture/banned.md` grows from α06a's about 1,000 words to about 3,000 common English words, and no word or phrase may spell one (A9.2).
2. `T17.2` **The syllable bank (`SND-03`, `PLT-03`, A13.9, A2.9).** `tools/voices.py` (new; run in the cloud, never in play) makes a virtual environment in the session's cache with `onnxruntime` and `numpy`, fetches Piper voices from `https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices` as B76's `setup.sh` and `speech.py` (`class Piper`) did (read with `git show <before>:pretests/b74-b76-sound-speech/<file>`, A2.9), and feeds IPA phoneme ids from each voice's own config directly, with no text front end.
   It speaks, inside carrier phrases, every half-syllable of the kept sounds of `data/culture/sounds.md`: each onset (none, a consonant, or one plus a liquid or glide) with each vowel, and each vowel with each coda (none or a consonant), stressed and unstressed, two takes each; it cuts each unit at the vowel's midpoint and keeps its pitch marks (an autocorrelation pitch tracker every 5 ms) and level: about 4,000 units a voice.
   It writes `assets/voices/<voice>-<version>.kdv`: a header, the unit table with marks, and 4-bit IMA ADPCM at 16 kHz, about 5 MB a voice, in the APK and beside the web build (A13.9); the banks are committed, so later sessions never fetch the voices, and the APK stays under 50 MB.
   Fallback, if strung half-syllables sound choppy: whole syllables with the 6 commonest codas, one take, about 6 MB a voice, A9.2 then drawing codas only from those.
3. `T17.3` **Choosing the voice (`SND-03`, `CUL-17`, `PRE-40`, A13.9, A15.4).** Candidates are Piper voices whose licence needs at most a credit, such as the speakers of `en_US-libritts_r-medium` (CC BY 4.0, B76) and other voices so licensed, large multilingual ones included, in pairs of a woman's and a man's base voice; for each, the count of A9.2's sounds it keeps, by B76's method (a sound counts as kept when it occurs in the voice's training language).
   `kd sound page` builds a private listening page (published as A15.4 publishes notes) with, for each pair, 10 strung phrases of one invented language beside the same phrases spoken whole by the model, and the kept count; the note links it, and you pick by ear, replying "voice: <name>".
   Until then the pair keeping the most sounds is used; the choice sets `voice_kept` in `data/culture/sounds.md` (`CUL-17`; every sound counts as kept until now, A9.2) and the voice's settings in `data/sounds/voice.md` (new), with its credit in `assets/LICENSES.md` and on α07b's credits screen (`PRE-40`).
   New worlds' languages draw only kept sounds (A9.2); a world made earlier voices each unkept sound as the kept sound of its class nearest in the IPA chart, listed as `nearest_kept` in `data/culture/sounds.md` (an addition to A9.2 for the murmur alone, written into the architecture in this branch).
4. `T17.4` **Stringing a world's phrases (`SND-03`, A13.9).** `string_voice(bank: &[u8], plan: &MurmurPlan, voice: BaseVoice, seed: u64) -> Phrases` in `crates/kd-audio/src/murmur/string.rs`, run by `kd-app` on the I/O thread when a world is made or loaded, or after a memory trim, for each base voice in turn, in under a second; on the web in slices of at most 4 ms a frame, shortest phrases first.
   For each of the plan's phrases: each syllable takes its halves by stress and its take by the world's seed; halves meet in the vowel with 15 ms crossfades at matching pitch marks; pitch-synchronous overlap-add sets each tag's contour and length (statements fall, questions rise at the end, calls rise and hold, soothing ones lower and slower, sharp ones short).
   The 400 phrases are held at 16 kHz, 16 bits (about 20 MB) with their syllable and pitch marks, sent to the mixer as `AddSample` 64 a frame (`Planner::murmur`), and never saved; critical `onTrimMemory` drops them until the next resume strings them again (A13.2).
5. `T17.5` **Talk (`CUL-24`, `SND-03`, `SND-07`, A13.9, A13.6).** `kd-sim` puts A13.6's `TalkView` (speakers, topic, times) in the snapshot from α06b's talk groups; `murmur/talk.rs` plays a talk as turns of 1–3 phrases with gaps of 0.3–0.8 s: a question topic takes a question phrase, a call a call, the rest statements (sharp and soothing phrases wait for feelings, α28); nobody repeats a phrase twice running.
   Voices (A13.9): each person speaks with the base voice of their sex, children with the woman's, shifted by resampling: children +3 semitones, elders −1 with a 5 Hz tremor of ±1.5%, ±1.5 semitones by height (`BIO-08`), ±1 by uid; plus a ±2 dB tilt by age and a personal ±2 dB peak at 1.2–2.4 kHz.
   Muffled: each voice through a 4 kHz low-pass, and the murmur bed, α16c's new bed kind (a speech-shaped wash plus phrase grains), through 1.5 kHz, before distance (tuned with you at the stage review); up to 4 voices sound singly, nearest first, the rest joining the murmur bed; at speed a talk under way is murmured at natural pace (`SND-07`).
6. `T17.6` **People's own sounds (`SND-03`, `PRE-18`, `SND-08`, A13.5, A13.6).** About 36 recordings join α16c's `data/sounds/recordings.md`, their files in `assets/sounds/` (A13.5): laughing, crying, calling and screaming for a child, a woman, a man and an elder, and babies' cries, never a word; public domain, CC0 or CC BY 4.0 only, found as α16c finds them, each with its file, author, source, licence, credit and level at 1 m, packed by `kd sound pack`; a kind with no clearly licensed recording takes the nearest code-made sound, named in the stage report (A13.5's fallback).
   Vocals (A13.6), made by the snapshot builder with no world state: a wound or a blow gives a scream; a shout or call (α10a's loud events) a call; play gives laughter, spaced by `kd-audio`'s own generator; a baby's need below 20, or pain of 60 or more, gives crying; each shifted like its speaker's voice; at the Plain and Gentle levels a scream plays as a call (`PRE-18`); a scream off screen keeps its direction (`SND-08`).
7. `T17.7` **The phone check, the reel, the demo world and delivery (`SND-01`, `SND-12`, `PRC-11`, A13.13, A13.14, A15.10, A15.11).** The stage's dearest sound scene, `a17-dearest` (32 sounds with distance, muffling and cave echo), joins α07d's phone benchmark (`kd-app/src/bench.rs`) as a sound phase: played live for 60 s, counting dropouts and mixing time into the `KDB1:` code (`SND-01`'s Done when, A13.13); over budget the cap falls to 24, then 16 (A13.3).

### α17b Everyday illnesses (about 5 hours)

**Goal:** colds and coughing fevers pass between people who share a hearth or nurse each other, gut sickness comes from water drunk below a camp, worms from raw meat, wound fever and lockjaw from wounds; the sick slow down and look ill, some die on their worst day, and fewer when someone cares for them.

**Tasks:**
1. `T17b.1` **The everyday illnesses as data (`BIO-05`, `MAT-13`, `MAT-17`, A7.13).** `kd-data`'s kind `Illness` and `data/illnesses/everyday.md` (new, A7.13), one entry each with `routes`, `incubation`, `course`, `contact_chance` (a day, per contact), `death` (for an untreated healthy adult), `slow`, `pain`, `immunity`, `starts` (a yearly rate in a band of 30, by season), `raw_meal`, `follows`, `crowd = false`, `effects` and `signs`, every length a game value (`TIM-18`: up to two weeks as in life, longer ones a sixth):
   - `cold`: breath and touch; signs in 1–2 days; about 5 days; harmless; immune for a game year; starts 3 a band-year;
   - `coughing_fever`: breath and touch; 1–3 days; about 7 days; kills 1 in 50; immune for 3 game years; starts 0.5 a band-year;
   - `chest_fever`: not catching; follows a cold or coughing fever in 1 in 10 babies, old (over 60) or hungry people and 1 in 100 others, and freezing (chill 80 or more for an hour) or a near-drowning in 1 in 5; 7–10 days; kills 1 in 4;
   - `gut_sickness`: fouled water (1 in 20 each day someone drinks it) and food handled by the sick; within a day; 2–5 days; kills 1 in 100; starts 0.3 a band-year;
   - `worms`: a raw or undercooked meal of meat or fish, `raw_meal` 1 in 100; condition −1 a day until medicine of 3 or more on 3 days running clears them (A8.4); never from cooked food;
   - `wound_fever`: an infected wound, 1 in 3 (A8.6), or a birth, 1 in 70; 1–3 days; 5–10 days; kills 1 in 3;
   - `lockjaw`: 1 in 20 cuts or bites of 20 or more from teeth, horn or a wooden point, or dirtied with earth or dung; 3–15 days; 10–20 days; kills 1 in 2;
   - `sore_eyes`: touch; 2–5 days; about 10 days; its contact chance doubled by a `smoky` hearth and in sleep groups of 20 or more (tuned); from a person's third bout, 1 in 5 scars an eye, a quarter off sight (`BIO-18`); starts 0.5 a band-year.

   **Near counts:** in each quarter-hour barrier's window phase a contagious being looks up those within about 3 m in its cluster's index of positions and counts them in its own row, the only row it writes (A7.13).
   **The daily job** (A4.9's illness row, 02:00, one job): contagious beings in uid order find their contacts, by breath their sleep group (`sleep_groups`: one roof or one hearth each night, A8.6) and those counted at 4 or more of the day's 96 barriers, by touch their `carers`, bed-sharers and those who ate food they handled (`ate_handled_by`), each rolling once a day a keyed pair draw at the contact chance (`illness.contact`, system 6, a pair purpose, fortune `Bad` for the one catching), from a day before the signs show until recovery, the immune never catching; then bands in uid order roll starts, each everyday illness at its yearly rate × band size ÷ 30 ÷ 60 a day, by season, in one keyed member (`illness.start`); then it creates the new rows, ends those past their end (immunity added) and removes the dead's.
   **Other routes** (T17b.3), met inside a cluster, roll there and post the new infection to the cluster's buffer, which the barrier merge adds in (time, uid, sequence) order (A4.8); each new row's days become Body events for that being, placed in its cluster (A7.13).
   α12b's `LifeWorld` gains `sleep_groups`, `carers` (α09b's), `ate_handled_by`, `risk` and `band_of` (α06a's `GroupView`), as A7.1 lists them.
   Purposes, system 6: `illness.contact`, `start`, `turn`, `death`, and `water` and `raw_meal` for catching by a drink and a meal (fortune `Bad`), the last two an addition to A7.14's list written into the architecture in this branch; the test switch `illness.starts` (no starts while off) is declared on α07c's `switches!` in `kd-life/src/purposes.rs` (`RES-10`, A3.9).
3. `T17b.3` **Water, food and wounds (`WLD-17`, `BIO-05`, A5.10, A6.4, A8.6).** `crates/kd-world/src/water/foul.rs` (A5.10, which puts fouled water at `MIL-03`): A5.2's sparse map `foul` marks running water within about 1 km downstream of a camp, a herd's crossing or a carcass lying in water, following α02a's cells' `flow`, while they are there and 3 days after, and still pools under about 50 m across while the local mean is 15 °C or more (tuned); springs and water above any camp stay clean.
   `kd-sim`'s daily cells job hands `foul.rs` the day's sources (the band records' camps, α12b's herd legs that cross water, carcasses lying in water), since `kd-world` cannot see people, animals or things (A2.2).
   **Food-handled marks** (A6.4's side map): gathering, butchering, cooking or carrying food marks it with the handler and the day, and eating a marked food is a touch contact with its handler.
   Drinking from foul water gives `gut_sickness` at 1 in 20 a day (`illness.water`); a raw or undercooked meal of meat or fish gives `worms` at 1 in 100 (`illness.raw_meal`), a meal in α14a's `cooked` state never; α09b's infected wounds (`kd_life::body`, which left wound fever to this alpha) turn to `wound_fever` at 1 in 3 when their infection is compared, and α06c's births at 1 in 70; a cut or bite of 20 or more from teeth, horn or a wooden point, or one α09b marked dirty, gives `lockjaw` at 1 in 20; `chest_fever` follows as its entry says (`illness.turn`).
4. `T17b.4` **The sick body, care, and who dies (`BIO-05`, `BIO-23`, `BIO-14`, `PRE-27`, A8.6, A7.13, A11.8).** While ill (`kd-people/src/body/illness.rs`, A8.6): work and walking at half speed with a fever and three quarters otherwise (`BIO-05`); the entry's pain (fever 10, chest fever 20, lockjaw 40); the thought `ill` (−6), or `gravely_ill` (−12) on and after the worst day of a deadly illness; and the look of illness, a paler skin step, the torso 8° forward and a slower pace, a variant added to A11.8's table and written into the architecture in this branch (`PRE-27`).
   **Who dies,** as A7.13 states it once: on the worst day one roll (`illness.death`, fortune `Bad`) at min(0.9, `death` × 5 for babies under 1 and people over 60 × 2 for each of hunger (condition under 30), real cold (10 °C or more below their limit, chill 40 or more, A8.3) and another wound (pain 20 or more from a wound other than the one the illness came from) × (1 + (average − resistance) ÷ average)), then × (0.5 − 0.025 × the carer's healing experience) if cared for that day, and × (1 − 0.1 × medicine taken that day); `risk_factors` (A8.6) supplies the inputs; survivors recover at the course's end, immune for the entry's time.
   **Care** (`BIO-23`): α09b's plain care (`body/care.rs`), drawn by the caring leaning, now also tends the sick (food, water, warmth and company), and an hour of it in a day adds the carer to `carers(who)`, counting as cared for at that carer's healing experience; the test switch `minds.care` (α07c's `switches!` in `kd-people/src/purposes.rs`, `RES-10`) removes the care option while off.
   A death goes through α06c's `Death`, its how in `data/text/deaths.md` reading like "coughing fever, caught from Tor" or "gut sickness, from foul water below the camp" (`BIO-14`).
5. `T17b.5` **Showing illness, the sign and outbreaks (`PRE-35`, `TIM-02`, `PRE-39`, A12.4, A10.7, A12.5, A8.6).** α04d's person card adds each illness with its day, such as "coughing fever, day 3 of about 7" (`PRE-35`).
   α11b's `badly_wounded` sign, "someone you follow badly wounded or gravely ill" (A10.7), now also posts when a followed person's deadly illness reaches its worst day (A8.6), its banner `sign_badly_wounded` in `data/text/moments.md` gaining illness phrasings; no new sign is added (A10.10).
   An outbreak, 5 or more of one band sick with one illness within 5 days (tuned), logs `outbreak` (α07b's event-kind table, kept forever and first-able, A7.14), so a people's first outbreak of each illness becomes a book entry through α11b's other-firsts recogniser (A12.5); α07b's table also gains `illness_caught`, `illness_shown` and `illness_ended` (logged, A7.14); `data/text/illness.md` (new) holds `outbreak`, `died_of_illness` and the card's illness line, 5 phrasings and a short form each.
   `World::record_kinds()` gains `life.infections`, `life.immunity`, `world.foul` and `things.handled`, with their `FINDABLE` lines (the person card's illness lines; the place card's water line, "fouled below the camp"; the thing card's handled line).
6. `T17b.6` **Scenes, the demo world and delivery (`BIO-05`, `BIO-23`, `PRC-11`).** Scene settings gain `ill = { who, illness, day }` and `immune = { who, illness }`, choosing only the start.

**On the phone:**
1. Open the alpha link; Make test world `a17b · Coughs in winter`, then open it from Worlds.
2. Tap a coughing person: their card reads "coughing fever, day 2 of about 7", and they move slowly, pale and hunched.
3. Watch a few game days at the camp stop's speed: others who sleep by the same hearth fall ill, and someone sits with the sickest, bringing water; their card says they are caring for them.
4. Follow the sickest: on their worst day time may slow, "gravely ill".
5. If someone dies, their card names the illness and who it was caught from.

**Not in this alpha:** illnesses from animals, foaming madness and hunter's fever, with the healing blueprints and medicine on purpose (α24a); herders' fever (α44); the crowd illnesses (α46b); `MOM-02`'s craft lost to a fever (its scene runs from Stage 4, α24b); the stage's close (α17c).

**Risks:** illness racing through a cave where 30 share one roof: contact chances are tuned on the tuning seeds against `BIO-05`'s yearly rates, while the death shares hold by construction (one roll on the worst day), and no scene is loosened (`RES-09`); the daily contact pass costly in big camps: one lookup per barrier per contagious being (A7.13), measured in the bench; fouled water marked too coarsely along the first region's single river: `foul` follows the cells' `flow` in 1 km steps, enough for "below the camp"; Stage 1 to 3 scenes meeting illness for the first time: they must still pass, any failure fixed in the tuned contact chances, never in a pass rule.

## Stage 4: A living world (MIL-04)

This stage turns the hand-set island into whole generated worlds you can zoom from one person to the globe, with weather, water, plants and herds alive everywhere, and gives people hunting, illness from animals and healing, burial, clothing and huts, plans with times, leaders and group plans, while your other weather powers and animal dreams arrive (`SCP-16`).
The brief's ten alphas hold about twice their hours of tasks, so they are split at natural seams: α18 in three; α19 in three, a whole world's saving (α19c) on its own; α20 in three, rivers, floods and seas (α20c) on their own; α23 in three, snares and fishing (α23b) and bark trays, hot stones and acorns (α23c) on their own; α22, α24, α25 and α26 in two; α27 in three, the stage's close (α27c) on its own; α21 stays whole: 24 alphas of about 119 hours against the brief's 10 and 43.
Built earlier and grown here, never rebuilt: the island's cells, B11's drainage (`gen/drain.rs`), rivers, caves, areas and ways (α02a–α03d), its kept areas (α04a), its plants (α02d, α05), wounds and care (α09b, α17b), herds, predators and kills (α12b), danger pairs, the stalk of a person and its sign, and small game (α12c), the sun and moon (α03a), weather, lightning and the climate record (α13), fire in camp and in the land with its disasters (α14a, α14b), the ring, dreams and the record of acts (α16), the mixer, the land heard and the murmur (α16b, α16c, α17) and the everyday illnesses and fouled water (α17b).
Homes for items the brief's list leaves out: the knowledge and craft overlays (`PRE-07`) in α19b; whole-world saving, dormant blocks and the memory pause in α19c; the moon in rules and eclipses (`WLD-07`, on α03a's sky) in α20a; gusts and quakes toppling stacks (`MAT-11`) in α20b, and huts in α25b; salt water (`BIO-09`) and the flood power in α20c; bark trays and boiling with hot stones (`MAT-18`), which Stage 3 left to this stage, in α23c, with leaching (`RCK-13`) and fermenting (`RCK-07`), whose timers A6.12 first needs at `MIL-04`; snares, fish traps and hook and line (A7.10's catching rows) in α23b, so Stage 7's fishing villages grow them instead of starting them; burial, the cut-away (`PRE-25`) and the lost-craft scene (`MOM-02`, due from `MIL-04`) in α24b; the first people's style and the 12 patterns (`PRE-43`, `CUL-12` in part) in α25b, as Stage 5 expects.
Each alpha's first phone step makes its demo world on the phone: a scene marked `demo = { name, run, at }`, compiled into the blob and built by the Tests screen's Make test world (α08's `kd-app/src/demo.rs`); the world-making alphas α18a–α18c use the Tests screen's world maker instead, and α27a and α27b New world; from α19a a scene may stand on a whole generated world (the setting key `generated`) or on land cut from one (`kd world cut`, into `scenes/lands/`).
Every alpha ends with its delivery: goldens, its `versionCode` by A15.3's formula (α18a 4181, α18b 4182, α18c 4183, α19a 4191, α19b 4192, α19c 4193, α20a 4201, α20b 4202, α20c 4203, α21 4210, α22a 4221, α22b 4222, α23 4230, α23b 4232, α23c 4233, α24a 4241, α24b 4242, α25a 4251, α25b 4252, α26a 4261, α26b 4262, α27a 4271, α27b 4272, α27c 4273), `bench/cloud/<alpha>.json` rows, then P0's steps 5 to 8; each new kind of record joins `World::record_kinds()` with its `FINDABLE` line, each new logged event α07b's `data/history/event_kinds.md`, each new moment or sign α11b's `data/director/`, and each chunk schema change brings its migration and fixture.
Each alpha keeps every earlier scene passing at its threshold (P0's definition of done, item 3), the island's `sharp-stone` test and its control (`RES-02`, `RES-03`) among them: island worlds keep their land, herds and climate, and of this half only α21's plant species and α19a's area rules reach the island.
Big updates (A3.6, A14.9): Stage 3 left `major = 5` and `generator = 6`; each change to generation, area-making or the kinds of rock, plant, animal or material in the land raises them: α18a to 6 and 7, α18b to 7 and 8, α18c to 8 and 9, α19a to 9 and 10, α20c `major` alone to 10 (salt water), α21 to 11 and 11, α22a to 12 and 12, and α27a, whose ranked start region is generation's step 12, to 13 and 13; the second half's other alphas change no generation and add no kind of rock, plant, animal or material to the land, so they are small updates, each chunk schema change with its migration and fixture.
Speed: the stage closes at 1.7 game years a real minute at 1,000 people (`PLT-04`) with the world alone at 10 or more (`TIM-07`); from α20a each alpha's cloud bench runs the world with nobody in it (seed 1) and reads the 1,000-person world against 1.7 by A16.3's model with the measured world layers, until α27b moves the bench worlds onto generated land.
History begins on generated worlds in α27b: the nightly pace test moves to generated worlds and judges clothing, huts and `RES-25` too (`RES-07`), and the bench worlds move onto generated land beside the world with nobody in it (`PLT-04`); the stage closes in α27c with the contact sheet, sound reel, stage budget, report and your review (`PRE-31`, `SND-12`, `RES-06`, `RES-22`).

### α18a Plates and ranges (about 5 hours)

**Goal:** a seed makes a whole wrap-around world of plates, rock layers, mountain ranges, volcano lines, faults, eroded valleys, seas and polar ice, which you open on the phone as a flat world map.

**Serves:** `WLD-09` (part: plates, rock, uplift and erosion), `WLD-06` (part: tilt, land share, plates and stars from the seed), `WLD-03`, `WLD-01` (part: the polar ice cap), `WLD-30` (part: heights), `WLD-15` (part: faults and volcanoes placed along plate edges), `WLD-08` (part: one seed, one world), `WLD-12` (part: the world-cell layer whole), `WLD-11` (part: generation timed), `SCP-12`, `PRE-29` (part: the world map look, flat), `PRE-13` (part: the world's numbers and features findable), `PLT-09` (part: a big update, marked).

**Architecture:** `A5.7`, `A5.2`, `A3.7`, `A3.3`, `A3.2`, `A2.2`, `A2.9`, `A14.1`, `A14.3`, `A14.9`, `A11.5`, `A12.4`, `A2.7`.

**Needs:** α17c (Stage 3 done), with α02a's world-cell columns (`FixedCells`), preset builder (`lands::build`), rock kinds, B11's drainage (`gen/drain.rs`) and `kd map preview`, α01b's relief port (`area/relief.rs`, `relief::key`), α03a's sky draws and header, α07a's chunks, `kd world` and fixtures, and α07d's Tests screen.

**Crates and files touched:** `kd-world` (`src/gen/mod.rs`, `src/gen/b11.rs`, `src/gen/plates.rs`, `src/gen/rock.rs`, `src/gen/uplift.rs`, `src/gen/features.rs`, `src/gen/erode.rs`, `src/gen/quality.rs`, all new; α02a's `src/gen/drain.rs`, `src/cells.rs` and `src/purposes.rs`), `kd-sim` (α03a's `src/world.rs`: the header's world numbers), `kd-save` (`world.fixed` per region, the header, migrations), `kd-tools` (`src/world.rs`: `kd world new` generating, `kd world check`; `src/map.rs`: `kd map preview` on a world folder), `kd-view` (`src/map.rs`: `MapTexture`), `kd-render` (`src/map.rs` new), `kd-ui` (`src/views/world_maker.rs` new, α07d's `src/views/tests.rs`, `src/findable.rs`), `kd-app` (`src/gen_job.rs` new), `data/world/rocks.md`, `data/palette/ladders.md`, `data/tuning/world.md`, `data/VERSION.toml`, `tests/golden/generator.toml`, `tests/fixtures/worlds/`.

**Tasks:**
1. `T18a.1` **Port B11's plates and erosion, and pass its hash (`WLD-09`, `WLD-08`, `TIM-16`, A2.9, A5.7, A3.2).** Recover `git show <before>:pretests/b04-b11-storage-terrain/phone/src/terrain.rs` and `.../src/data.rs`, `<before>` being `$(git log --diff-filter=D --format=%H -1 -- pretests/BUILDING-BLOCKS.md)^`, after `git fetch --unshallow origin` when `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` prints `true` (A2.9); while `pretests/` still stands, read it in place; name the source in the commit.
   α01b ported B11's metre-detail half (`area/relief.rs`: `grad`, `fade`, `noise`, `fbm`, with B11's `key` and `mix` kept as `relief::key` and a test copy of `data::hash`), and α02a its `fill`, `receivers` and `drainage` (`gen/drain.rs`); this task ports the rest of the world half on top of both, re-porting none of them: `set_sea_level` and `erode` into `gen/erode.rs`, calling `gen/drain.rs`; `gen_plates` into `gen/plates.rs` as `b11_plates`; `map_hash` and `quality` into `gen/quality.rs`, the slopes in `f32` through `kd_core::m::atan` (A3.2 bans `f64` outside `kd-tools` and test statistics); `gen/b11.rs` holds only the port check.

   `b11_plates(7, 1024, 512)` (B11's own seed, size and 14 plates) must give `map_hash` `895e636495687a48` on `Serial` and on 4 `Workers`; if a replaced call moves a bit, per-step hashes find it, and only a signed-zero difference may be fixed (A3.2).
2. `T18a.2` **The generator's frame and the world numbers, step 0 (`WLD-06`, `WLD-08`, `SCP-12`, A5.7, A3.3, A3.7).** `gen::generate<P: Pool>(seed: u64, version: u32, cat: &Catalogue, res: Res, upto: Step, pool: &P) -> GenWorld` (A5.7's call, with the step to stop after and the pool), where `Res` is `Km1` (2,000 × 1,000 cells of 1,024 m, A3.7) or `Km2` (1,000 × 500, for α27a's first pass); `GenWorld` holds `WorldNumbers`, `FixedCells` (A5.2's 32 bytes a cell), the side tables, and scratch fields kept only while the maker is open; it runs only `WLD-09`'s stages, in order (`SCP-12`).
   New purposes of system 1 in α02a's `crates/kd-world/src/purposes.rs` (A3.3): `gen.tilt`, `gen.land`, `gen.plates`, `gen.plate_site`, `gen.velocity`, `gen.block`, `gen.rock`, `gen.feature`, `gen.peak`, `gen.stars`, each keyed on the world's place uid, or the plate's, block's or edge segment's, at moment 0, fortune `None`.
   `WorldNumbers { tilt_deg (uniform 15–30), land_share (0.25–0.50), plates (6–12), peak_m (3,000–4,500), sky: Sky, stars: u64 }` (`WLD-06`); the `Sky` is drawn by α03a's sky draws (`moon_start` over a season, `node_period` and `node_start` in `[sky]`'s ranges), keyed on the world's place uid, with the drawn tilt, and checked over generated worlds in α20a; α03a's header and `meta.bin` gain the numbers (A3.9).
   The island keeps `lands::build`, and each island world keeps the fixed layers it saved (A5.6), so the generator never moves land under its people.
3. `T18a.3` **Plates and older blocks, step 1 (`WLD-09`, `WLD-06`, A5.7, A3.7).** `gen/plates.rs` grows B11's Voronoi to `numbers.plates` keyed sites on the torus, distances wrapped both ways (A3.7 `wrap`), edges warped by two fbm offsets at 256 km and 64 km periods (B11's `qx`, `qy`).
   Each plate gets B11's rational-circle direction (no trigonometry) times a speed of 1–5 cm a year (`gen.velocity`) and a crust: plates are made continental largest first until their area reaches the land share + 10%, so shelves and lowlands drown the rest at sea level.
   Inside each continental plate, 3–6 older blocks (keyed sites, a Voronoi within the plate) give worn ranges on their joins (+300–800 m) and basins in their middles (−100–300 m) (A5.7).
   Scratch per cell: plate, nearest-edge distance in km, the plate across that edge, convergence (B11's `conv`, positive when closing) and block with its join distance.
4. `T18a.4` **Geology classes and rock layers, step 2 (`WLD-09`, A5.7).** `gen/rock.rs` sets each cell's `geo` class from its setting: `sea_floor` (oceanic crust), `volcanic_line` (the overriding plate 50–250 km from a convergent edge with an oceanic plate, or within 30 km of a rift), `folded_range` (within 150 km of a convergent edge between continental plates, or on a block join), `rift` (a divergent edge in continental crust), `basin` (block middles and continental shelves), else `old_worn`.
   `data/world/rocks.md` grows from α02a's five kinds to `WLD-09`'s twelve, adding `basalt`, `lava_ash`, `glassy_lava`, `shale`, `limestone` (caves true), `quartzite` and `slate`, each with α02a's and α02c's fields (softness, beds, caves, ladder, soft share, tone) and a ladder in `data/palette/ladders.md` only where none of α01a's fits; `quartzite` names α08's `quartzite_cobble` as its loose item, as α08's rocks name theirs, and basalt's and glassy lava's loose stones join with α18c's items.
   Rock, top first, by class (A5.7), each choice keyed with `gen.rock` on the block or edge segment so whole districts share it: `old_worn` sandstone or quartzite over granite or slate; `basin` chalk (40%) or limestone, then shale, then sandstone; `folded_range` slate, quartzite and folded limestone, granite in the cores (cells over 2,000 m after T18a.5); `volcanic_line` lava and ash, glassy lava within 20 km of a sticky volcano (T18a.6), basalt, granite; `rift` and `sea_floor` basalt over sandstone.
   `layer_m` holds the top two layers' thickness in 2 m steps, 4–60 m, keyed per district; river gravel and silt are laid by α18b's floodplains and fans.
5. `T18a.5` **Uplift and heights, step 3 (`WLD-09`, `WLD-30`, A5.7).** `gen/uplift.rs` applies B11's rule with the plate fields: continental +300 m, oceanic −3,200 m blended across edges, convergent `+conv × 4,200 × bump` (× 0.7 between ocean and continent), rifts `conv × 900 × bump`, the blocks' joins and basins, ridge noise × bump × 1,500 m and broad inland relief of ±400 m (A5.7's fix for B11's flat continents).
   Then `set_sea_level` at the land share, and a monotone piecewise-linear remap of land heights fitted so the highest cell is `numbers.peak_m` and at least 80% of land lies below 1,000 m (`WLD-30`); sea depths are kept.
6. `T18a.6` **Faults and volcanoes (`WLD-15`, `WLD-30`, A5.2, A5.7).** `gen/features.rs`: faults along convergent and transform edges of continental crust as segments of 20–60 km (keyed) following the edge line, and volcanoes on volcanic lines every 30–80 km, `Sticky` (setting glassy lava nearby, so obsidian in α18c) where ocean meets continent and `Runny` at rifts and at 1–3 keyed hot spots, at most 1,000 features in all (A5.2's side table).
   `Feature { kind: Thrust | Strike | Normal | Sticky | Runny, cells, yearly_chance, quiet_years: (u16, u16), last: u32 }` with starting rates in `[features]` set near Earth's yearly rates for the same area (`WLD-15`, `WLD-30`): thrust 1/400, strike 1/250, normal 1/600 a game year a segment, quiet 50–300 years; runny 1/60, sticky 1/200, quiet 20–500 years (tuned in α20b); each cell on a feature takes its id in `feature`.
7. `T18a.7` **Erosion, polar ice and relief, steps 4 and 6's heights (`WLD-09`, `WLD-01`, A5.7, A5.2).** Run B11's `erode` on α02a's drainage: 3 rounds of priority-flood `fill`, `receivers`, `drainage` and implicit stream power with k = 0.004 × softness (shale, chalk, ash 2; sandstone, limestone 1.2; slate, quartzite 0.8; granite, basalt 0.5) × a rough rain (× 1.5 within 200 km of sea, × 0.6 beyond 800 km, × 0.5 at 20–35° latitude), then 2 hillslope passes, and a last fill that marks lake cells instead of raising them (α18b turns them into lakes).
   Every cell within 100 km of the seam row becomes ice (water flag `glacier`, heights kept), so the cap is about 200 km wide across the seam and nothing will cross its middle (`WLD-01`).
   `rough` (A5.2: 4 m steps of height spread inside a cell, read by α01b's relief) = clamp(2 + 30 × slope + 20 × ridge, 0, 255).

- Unit, `crates/kd-world/tests/gen_plates.rs`: `b11_plate_hash_reproduced` (`895e636495687a48`, 1 and 4 workers); `one_seed_one_world` (twice, and on 1 and 4 workers: equal hashes of `FixedCells` and the side tables, `WLD-08`); `world_is_2000_by_1000_cells` (`WLD-03`); `world_numbers_in_range_and_spread` (100 seeds: tilt 15–30°, land 25–50%, 6–12 plates, each quarter of each range drawn at least 10 times, `WLD-06`'s Done when); `land_share_matches_its_draw` (within 0.5%); `heights_keep_wld30` (20 worlds: highest land 3,000–4,500 m, at least 80% of land below 1,000 m); `ranges_volcanoes_faults_on_plate_edges` (20 worlds: at least 95% of land above 2,000 m within 150 km of a convergent edge or a block join, every volcano within 300 km of a convergent edge or on a rift or hot spot, every fault within 30 km of a plate edge; `WLD-09`'s Done when, first part); `chalk_and_limestone_only_in_basins_and_ranges` (`WLD-09`'s Done when, second part); `polar_ice_200_km_wide` (every cell within 100 km of the seam is ice, none beyond 120 km).
- `crates/kd-save/tests/fixed.rs`: `world_fixed_round_trip` (a 2 km world saved and read back byte-equal); `island_fixed_migrates` (`a17b.kindling`'s `world.fixed`, read through the migration, equals its island).
- α07a's `fixtures.rs`: `a18a.kindling` opens and runs a game day; Stage 3's fixtures open read-only with their books.

- Bench (A15.10): steps 0–4 at 1 km within 4 s on a cloud core and 1 s at 2 km, peak scratch memory within 400 MB.
- Screenshots (A15.11): the world maker at seeds 1 and 2, Height and Rock, portrait and landscape.

**On the phone:**
1. Install the alpha's APK or open its link; in Settings, long-press the version line to open Tests, then tap World maker.
2. Tap New: each step is named as it runs, and within about 20 seconds a whole world appears as a flat map: continents, ranges, seas shading to deep blue, and white polar ice along the top and bottom edges.
3. Drag the map off one side: the land comes back from the other.
4. Turn on Plates and faults: ranges and red volcano dots follow the plate lines; tap a mountain: its card says its height, its rock layers and "folded range".
5. Type seed 7 and tap New twice: the same world and summary both times; seed 8 differs.

**Not in this alpha:** rivers, lakes, caves, shores and currents (α18b); climate, soils, deposits and biomes (α18c); living on a generated world (α19a); the globe and the zoom out to it (α19b).

**Risks:** B11's flat continents with straight edges: older blocks and two-scale warping break them up, judged on α18c's contact sheet of 20 worlds, with A5.7's fallback (B11's erosion over warped noise, which passed every number); the port moving B11's hash: per-step hashes find the step, and only a signed-zero fix is allowed; memory on the phone during generation (scratch about 300 MB at 1 km): freed when the maker closes, measured by the bench; the web's pauses between steps: the maker is a test tool, and no play generates a world on the web before α27a.

### α18b Rivers, lakes and coasts (about 4.5 hours)

**Goal:** the generated world gets its rivers and streams on fixed courses, its lakes, marshes, springs, floodplains, caves, cliffs, shores and ocean currents, drawn on the world map, and meets `WLD-08`'s numbers over 20 worlds.

**Serves:** `WLD-09` (part: waters, landforms and caves), `WLD-08` (part: rivers reaching sea or lake, slopes, coasts, lakes), `WLD-17` (part: rivers, lakes, springs and marshes placed at generation), `WLD-26` (part: shelves, shores, currents and upwelling), `WLD-12` (part: each river's line fixed at generation, rivers never break), `WLD-24` (part: caves sized for bands), `PRE-26` (part: rivers on the map), `RES-16` (part: tuned on tuning seeds), `PRE-13` (part: lakes and stretches findable), `PLT-09` (part: a big update, marked).

**Architecture:** `A5.7`, `A5.2`, `A5.3`, `A5.10`, `A5.12`, `A11.5`, `A11.6`, `A14.9`.

**Needs:** α18a, with α02a's river-cell rows, `river_rating`, cave records and springs for the island (A5.6), α02b's area skeleton and α02c's cave chambers.

**Crates and files touched:** `kd-world` (`src/gen/waters.rs`, `src/gen/landforms.rs`, `src/gen/seas.rs`, all new; `src/gen/quality.rs`; α02a's `src/cells.rs` side tables), `kd-save` (the lake table in `world.fixed`), `kd-render` (`src/map.rs`: rivers, lakes, shores), `kd-ui` (`src/views/world_maker.rs`, `src/findable.rs`), `kd-tools` (preview layers, `kd world check --waters`), `data/tuning/world.md`, `data/TUNING-LOG.md`, `data/VERSION.toml`, `tests/golden/generator.toml`, `tests/fixtures/worlds/`.

**Tasks:**
1. `T18b.1` **Rivers and stretches (`WLD-09`, `WLD-08`, `WLD-12`, `WLD-17`, A5.7, A5.2).** From step 4's receivers and drainage (a 1 km cell is 1.049 km²), every land cell draining 50 km² or more is a river cell (`WLD-08`'s threshold); each river is walked from its sources down the receivers and cut into stretches of at most 10 km, and at every confluence and lake: `Stretch { id, cells, length_m, slope, drainage_km2, rating }`, the rating α02a's `river_rating` grown into a power law through its point (18 m wide and 1.2 m deep at 8 m³/s): bankfull width 18 m × (Q ÷ 8 m³/s)^0.5 and depth 1.2 m × (Q ÷ 8)^0.33, from a mean flow Q estimated from drainage × α18a's rough rain (tuned; α20c's routing uses it).
   Each river cell's row in α02a's river-cell table (A5.2) holds its stretch, an entry point on the edge toward its main upstream neighbour (a keyed spring point inside a source cell), an exit point on the edge toward its receiver, each a position along the edge keyed on the pair of cells so both cells agree, and bankfull width and depth; `river` holds the row.
   These are the rows α02b's skeleton (A5.3) already joins by its keyed meander, so generated rivers run through areas unchanged (`WLD-12`); the island keeps its own numbers.
2. `T18b.2` **Streams, springs and marshes (`WLD-17`, `WLD-09`, A5.7, A5.10).** Cells draining 2–50 km² are streams: `river` holds their drainage in km² (A5.2), and α02b's crossing sits on the edge toward `flow`, keyed on the pair.
   Springs (`WLD-17`): at slope feet, where an uphill neighbour is 60 m higher or more and permeable rock (sandstone, limestone, chalk, gravel) lies over impermeable (shale, slate, granite, clay), and in 1 in 8 limestone and chalk cells (keyed); water flag `spring`, as α02a's.
   Marshes on flat ground (slope under 0.1°) that drains badly: draining 20 km² or more within 2 cells of a river or lake, or below a spring, and 1 in 3 lake shores (keyed); water flag `marsh` (A5.10).
3. `T18b.3` **Lakes (`WLD-17`, `WLD-08`, A5.7, A5.10).** Each run of cells the last fill marked becomes `Lake { id, cells, sill_m, area_by_level: [(f32, f32); 8], outlet: Option<StretchId>, closed: bool }` in a new side table saved with `world.fixed`, closed when it has no outlet in a land whose rough rain is under 300 mm a year (A5.10's salt lakes, α20c); a lake under 1 km² stays a water flag only, its cells marshy; `lake` holds the id.
4. `T18b.4` **Landforms (`WLD-09`, `WLD-27`, A5.7).** Floodplains: cells beside a stretch draining 1,000 km² or more, sloping under 0.3° and within 2 km and 20 m of the river's level, get a top layer of silt (river gravel within 30 km of a range) 2–8 m thick and the flag `floodplain`; fans: where a river leaves a slope over 3° for one under 1°, the cells within 5 km below get river gravel; deltas: a stretch draining 5,000 km² or more that meets the sea spreads silt over 3–12 sea cells at its mouth in a keyed lobe, raised to 1 m above sea; glacial valleys: river cells above 2,500 m beyond 35° latitude get their floors widened (`rough` × 0.7) and their lakes kept (A5.7).
   Where a valley is cut deeper than the top layer (`layer_m[0]`), the cell's `exposed` bit shows the second layer in its banks, so α18c's deposits there show.
5. `T18b.5` **Cliffs, caves and shelters (`WLD-09`, `WLD-24`, A5.7, A5.3, A5.12).** Escarpments (`cliff`: the steepest step's direction and its height in 2 m steps) where hard rock (granite, basalt, quartzite, sandstone, limestone, chalk) caps softer rock and the step to a neighbour is 15 m or more (tuned); α19a's skeleton draws them with at least one gap a cell at the lowest point, where walks pass (A5.12).
   Caves in α02a's cave records (count 0–3, size, kind cave, lava tube or shelter, a dry bit): in limestone and chalk with relief of 40 m or more at 1 in 6 cells, lava tubes in lava and ash at 1 in 20, shelters under hard caps at 1 in 3 escarpment cells (keyed); dry unless the cell is a river cell, a marsh or holds a spring; sizes in four classes, about 8, 14, 22 and 30 m deep, holding about 10, 20, 40 and 60 people, from which α02c's 2–6 chambers are sized.
6. `T18b.6` **Seas, shelves, shores and currents, step 6 (`WLD-26`, `WLD-01`, A5.7).** Sea cells within 30 km of land are lifted to −50 to −200 m by distance (shelves); each coastal land cell gets a shore kind in `geo`'s shore bits: beach (slope under 1°, no river mouth), rock (slope 3° or more, or a cliff), estuary (a river mouth), salt marsh (slope under 0.3° beside an estuary or delta).
   Oceans are sea bodies over 1 million km² (a flood fill on the torus, never across the polar ice); in each, sea cells within 300 km of its western shore take `sea_warm` +1 to +4 °C (warm currents running poleward, strongest at 20–40°), those within 300 km of its eastern shore −1 to −4 °C, and those within 100 km of its eastern shore between 10° and 40° latitude are marked `upwelling`, where α22a puts the most fish (`WLD-26`); enclosed seas take 0.
7. `T18b.7` **Water on the map (`PRE-26`, `PRE-29`, A11.5, A11.6).** `MapTexture`'s water flags gain river, stream, lake, marsh, spring and shore kind; `kd-render/src/map.rs` draws rivers as lines from the river-cell table, at least one art pixel wide where they drain 1,000 km² or more and wider with drainage (`PRE-26`, tuned), lakes in the lake ladder, marshes stippled and shores in their colours.
   The world maker gains chips Water and Shores, and its cell card the stretch, drainage, width, lake, cave and spring lines; `kd map preview` gains `--layer water|shores|caves`.
8. `T18b.8` **The `WLD-08` numbers, rivers through areas and delivery (`WLD-08`, `WLD-12`, `RES-16`, `PLT-09`, `PRC-11`, A5.7, A14.9).** `gen/quality.rs` grows B11's `quality` into `world_quality(&GenWorld) -> WorldQuality`: the share of river cells whose path reaches sea or a lake, the median land slope, the share of land over 30°, the longest straight coast (traced along cell edges; a run is straight while each edge stays within one cell of the line from the run's start) and lakes' share of land; `kd world check --waters --worlds 20 --base-seed 1000` prints them per world and fails outside `WLD-08`'s ranges.
   A missed number is tuned (`[waters]` and `[gen]`: the last fill's least lake depth and area, the rough-rain factors, the warp) on tuning seeds 1–20, logged in `data/TUNING-LOG.md` (`RES-16`), and checked on seeds 1000–1019.
   `World::record_kinds()` gains `world.lakes` and `world.stretches`, with their `FINDABLE` lines (the world maker's cell card; the place card's water line from α19a).
   The golden world moves to step 6; new waters, landforms and a new side table make this a big update: `major = 7`, `generator = 8`, earlier worlds opening read-only (`PLT-09`); fixture `a18b.kindling` (an island world, its lake table empty).
   Goldens `world-water-seed-1` and `world-shores-seed-2`; `versionCode=4182`, `versionName=a18b`; `bench/cloud/a18b.json` adds steps 5–6 at 1 km (A5.7: about 0.7 s of a cloud core); then P0's steps 5 to 8.

**Data:**
- `data/tuning/world.md`: `[waters]` (river 50 km², stream 2 km², stretch 10 km, the rating's exponents 0.5 and 0.33, springs 60 m and 1 in 8, marsh slope 0.1°, floodplain 1,000 km² and 0.3°, fans 3° to 1° and 5 km, deltas 5,000 km², glacial 2,500 m beyond 35°, escarpment step 15 m, caves 1 in 6, 1 in 20 and 1 in 3, cave sizes 8–30 m), `[seas]` (shelf 30 km at −50 to −200 m, current band 300 km at ±1–4 °C, upwelling within 100 km at 10–40°).
- `data/VERSION.toml`: `major = 7`, `generator = 8`; `tests/golden/generator.toml`: seed 1 through step 6; `tests/fixtures/worlds/a18b.kindling`.

**Tests:**
- Unit, `crates/kd-world/tests/gen_waters.rs`: `river_points_agree_across_cells` (every river cell's exit equals its receiver's entry over all rivers of 5 worlds); `every_river_ends_in_sea_or_lake`; `stretches_at_most_10_km`; `rating_meets_the_islands_point` (18 m and 1.2 m at 8 m³/s); `stream_crossings_face_flow`; `springs_only_at_slope_feet_or_karst`; `lakes_hold_sill_and_outlet`; `deltas_only_at_big_mouths`; `caves_only_in_karst_lava_or_under_caps` (`WLD-09`); `currents_warm_west_cold_east` (each ocean of 20 worlds: mean `sea_warm` within 300 km of its western shore above its eastern, `WLD-26`).
- `world_quality_numbers` (`WLD-08`'s Done when, but for your look in α18c): over seeds 1000–1019, at least 95% of rivers draining 50 km² reach sea or a lake, median land slope 0.5–5°, under 1% of land over 30°, no coast straight for over 20 km, lakes 1–3% of land.
- `areas_meet_on_generated_rivers`: α02b's skeleton and ground, unchanged, on 200 areas along seed 1's generated rivers: shared edge heights equal exactly and river beds run unbroken through every area (`WLD-12`'s "neighbouring areas meet within about 0.5 m; rivers never break").
- Golden: seed 1 through step 6; fixture `a18b.kindling` opens and runs a game day, and `a18a.kindling` opens read-only with its book (`PLT-09`).
- Bench: steps 5–6 at 1 km within 1.5 s on a cloud core.
- Screenshots: the world maker's Water and Shores at seeds 1 and 2.

**On the phone:**
1. Open the alpha link; in Settings long-press the version line, tap World maker, then New with seed 1.
2. Rivers now run from the ranges to the sea or to lakes, thicker downstream, with lakes and marshes among them.
3. Turn on Shores: beaches, rocky coasts, estuaries and salt marshes in their own colours.
4. Tap a big river near its mouth: its card gives its drainage in km², its stretch and its width; tap a limestone hill: "caves: 2, dry".
5. Pan along a coastline: it never runs long and straight.

**Not in this alpha:** how much water rivers carry day by day, floods and lakes rising (α20c); soil water, springs running and ice (α20a); climate, soils, deposits and biomes (α18c); generated cliffs, lakes and shores drawn in areas (α19a).

**Risks:** too many or too few lakes after the last fill: the least lake depth and area are tuned on tuning seeds; rivers running into the polar ice: the seam rows are closed to rivers, which end at the ice's edge; cliffs everywhere in rough ranges: the 15 m step and the hard-over-soft rule keep them to cap rocks, judged on the map.

### α18c Climate, soils, deposits and biomes (about 5 hours)

**Goal:** every place of the generated world gets its climate season by season, its soil, its flint, clay, ochre and ore where geology puts them, and its biome and plant cover, shown as layers on the world map and reviewed by you on a sheet of 20 worlds.

**Serves:** `WLD-16` (part: the climate and its record; Earth's climates in Earth's shares), `WLD-14`, `WLD-27` (part: soils and fertility at generation), `WLD-09` (part: climate, soils, deposits, biomes and cover in order), `WLD-31` (part: biomes and cover shares), `WLD-26` (part: warm and cold coasts in the climate), `WLD-01` (part: seasons reversed between the halves), `WLD-08` (part: your review of 20 worlds), `WLD-11` (part: one world timed on the phone), `MAT-10` (part: two new stones), `GOD-05` (part: each place's worst year, for the powers' caps), `PRE-13` (part: the runoff findable), `PLT-09` (part: a big update, marked).

**Architecture:** `A5.7`, `A5.8`, `A5.10`, `A5.11`, `A5.2`, `A5.3`, `A7.4`, `A3.7`, `A11.5`, `A14.9`, `A15.10`.

**Needs:** α18b, with α02a's climate record (`kd_world::climate`) as α13 grew it (about 100 bytes a weather cell, with its worst year), α13's storm calibration (`weather::calibrate` in `src/weather/storms.rs`), α02a's soils, deposits and biomes for the island (A5.6), α05's cover curves, α02d's species mix, and α08's stone items with the rocks' and deposits' item names.

**Crates and files touched:** `kd-world` (`src/gen/climate.rs`, `src/gen/soils.rs`, `src/gen/deposits.rs`, `src/gen/biomes.rs`, `src/water/runoff.rs`, all new; α02a's `src/climate.rs`: the record filled for generated worlds; α13's `src/weather/storms.rs`: calibration over the whole world), `kd-life` (α05's `src/plants/cover.rs`: cover from a drawn last disturbance), `kd-sim` (`GenLifeImpl`, α18c's `GenLife` over `kd-life`), `kd-save` (climate records and the runoff table in `world.fixed`), `kd-render` (`src/map.rs` cover classes), `kd-ui` (`src/views/world_maker.rs`, `src/findable.rs`), `kd-tools` (preview layers, `kd world check --climate --deposits`), `kd-app` (α07d's `src/bench.rs`: the world line), `tools/worldsheet.sh` new, `data/world/rocks.md`, `data/world/deposits.md`, `data/world/biomes.md`, `data/items/stone.md`, `data/tuning/world.md`, `data/VERSION.toml`, `tests/golden/generator.toml`, `tests/fixtures/worlds/`.

**Tasks:**
1. `T18c.1` **The climate record, step 7 (`WLD-16`, `WLD-26`, `WLD-01`, `GOD-05`, A5.7, A5.8, A3.7).** `gen/climate.rs` works per weather cell (200 × 100, A3.7) and season:
   - warmth: the season's mean daily sunlight at the cell's latitude from `kd_core::sky` at the world's tilt (day length and noon height averaged over its 15 days), mapped to sea-level warmth by a line fitted in `[climate]` so the year mean is about 27 °C at the equator, 12 °C at 45° and −5 °C at 65° at Earth's tilt; the seasonal swing × continentality (0.3 over sea, 0.6 on coasts, 1.0 beyond 1,000 km inland), sea lagging land by a third of a season; −6 °C per 1,000 m of the weather cell's mean land height (its reference height); + `sea_warm` within 300 km downwind of a current (`WLD-26`);
   - wind: belts by latitude moving ±5° with the sun (trade easterlies to 30°, westerlies to 60°, polar easterlies beyond), speed by belt;
   - rain: a moisture march along each row in the wind's direction, two laps round the torus from its most windward sea cell: air gains moisture over sea by sea warmth, drops 0.1 of it a cell and more where it climbs (× 1.5 per 100 m of rise), times belt factors (× 1.5 near the equator, × 0.4 at 20–35°, × 1.2 at 45–60°, × 0.5 beyond 65°), so the windward side of a range is wet and its lee dry;
   - from these: snow share, storm and thunder days (thunder where the season is warm, over 15 °C, and moist), the longest usual dry spell, cold-outbreak days, humidity, cloud, daily range (wider dry and inland, narrow on coasts), record low and high at the mean ∓ 2.5 spreads, and the worst year by α13's factors (1.5 × the storm days and the dry spell, 1.6 × the rain, the record low), which α20b's caps and worst-year test read (`GOD-05`).
   The record is α02a's `Climate` (`kd-world/src/climate.rs`) as α13 grew it, about 100 bytes a weather cell (A5.8), one per weather cell and season, the type `lands::build` fills for the island, so the hourly step reads one type; per world cell, `clim` holds the warmth offset from height against the reference (0.25 °C steps) and a rain factor from aspect to the wind, and `hollow` the cold-air pooling (lower than all 8 neighbours by 10 m or more) and aspect.
2. `T18c.2` **Storm calibration and the runoff table (`WLD-16`, `WLD-17`, A5.8, A5.10).** α13's `weather::calibrate` (`src/weather/storms.rs`, A5.8) runs over all 20,000 weather cells: fronts born over sea cells and showers anywhere, each birth cell's mean path traced on the season's winds, birth rates scaled by (target ÷ traced storm-hours)^½ for 8 rounds, then rain per storm-hour = the season's rain ÷ traced storm-hours, so long-run rain matches each place's climate; the paths wrap east–west and end at the polar ice instead of a void.
   `kd-world/src/water/runoff.rs`: the runoff table maps each weather cell to the stretches its land drains into, with each one's share by area (A5.10), for α20c's routing.
   Both are kept with the record in `world.fixed` (A5.8); α13's fallback holds: a land cell outside ±20% after 8 rounds takes rain per place from its climate alone, storms only for timing, counted in `kd world check --climate`.
3. `T18c.3` **Soils, step 8 (`WLD-27`, A5.11).** α02a's soils (`data/world/soils.md`'s eight kinds, A5.11) placed over the whole world: silt on floodplains and deltas; sand on beaches, dunes and sandstone in dry lands; loam on shale, limestone and granite in mild, wet climates; clay where granite or shale rots in warm, wet climates and on old lake beds; peat on marshes and cold, wet flats; ash within 30 km of volcanoes; stony on slopes over 15° and on gravel; thin on bare heights.
   Base fertility (0–5 in steps of 1/40) high on silt, ash and wind-blown dust (within 200 km downwind of dry lands under 250 mm a year and of the ice), low on sand, steep slopes, peat and where over 2,000 mm of rain meets a year mean over 22 °C (washed out), and +1 on grassland once T18c.5 has set the biomes; `soil`, `soil_base`, and the changing `fertility` starting at the base (A5.2, `WLD-27`).
4. `T18c.4` **Deposits, step 9 (`WLD-14`, `MAT-10`, `MAT-06`, A5.7, A5.3).** α02a's deposits (`flint_in_chalk`, `river_gravel`, `WLD-14`) placed over the whole world, two (kind, richness 1–5) pairs a cell and a rare third in the side table: flint nodules in chalk (1 in 2 chalk cells), chert in limestone (1 in 5); obsidian in glassy lava within 20 km of a sticky volcano; hammer and grinding stones where quartzite, basalt or sandstone shows (top or exposed); clay in the banks of rivers draining 200 km² or more, in 1 in 4 floodplain cells (old river bends), on lake beds and in clay soils over granite; red and yellow ochre where sandstone or basalt weathers in warm climates (1 in 30, keyed); green and blue copper ore in volcanic lines within 50 km of granite (1 in 200 cells), with native copper as the third deposit in 1 in 10 of those.
   River gravel then carries hard stones (flint, chert, quartzite, basalt, obsidian) downstream in one pass in drainage order, each one's share × 0.8 every 10 km as α02a's island gravel falls, so flint turns up in gravels far from its chalk (A5.7).
   They show only where the land is cut (banks, cliffs, cave walls, scree, gravel bars, bare rock), as α08's stone patches in `kd-world/src/area/contents.rs` already read, and deeper ones only by digging (`MAT-06`).
   As α08 does for the island, deposits name the items their stone patches yield in `data/world/deposits.md`, and rocks their loose and boulder items in `data/world/rocks.md`: `data/world/deposits.md` gains `chert_in_limestone` (α08's `chert_nodule`), `obsidian`, `hard_stone` (α08's `quartzite_cobble` and `sandstone_cobble`, and `basalt_cobble`), `clay`, `ochre`, `copper_ore` and `native_copper`; `basalt` names `basalt_cobble` and `glassy_lava` `obsidian_lump`; `data/items/stone.md` gains those two with all 18 characteristics (`MAT-10`): `basalt_cobble` (a hammer and grinding stone) and `obsidian_lump` (flaking 5, toughness 1); limestone, shale, slate and lava and ash shed no loose item until an alpha needs one, their exposures drawn as scree; clay, ochre and copper yield nothing until the alphas that first use them add their items (α41, α33, α47b).
5. `T18c.5` **Biomes and cover, step 10 (`WLD-31`, `WLD-09`, A5.7, A7.4).** `gen/biomes.rs` gives each land cell, in this order: ice (glacier); shore (beach or salt-marsh coasts, and rocky coasts with thin or stony soil); marsh (the flag); mountain heights (warmest season under 10 °C only because of height); tundra (warmest under 10 °C); desert (under 250 mm a year); tropical forest (year mean 20 °C or more, 1,500 mm or more, dry season under 60 days); savanna (year mean 20 °C or more, otherwise); dry scrub (250–600 mm with a warm dry season of 30 days or more and the coldest season above 0 °C); northern conifer forest (coldest season under −5 °C, 300 mm or more); grassland (under 750 mm); else broadleaf forest; thresholds in `[biomes]`.
   `data/world/biomes.md` grows from α02a's five (`broadleaf_forest`, `grassland`, `marsh`, `shore`, `sea`, beside its test biome `barren`) by `tropical_forest`, `savanna`, `dry_scrub`, `desert`, `conifer_forest`, `tundra`, `mountain_heights` and `ice`, each with its mature shares and its fire and flood interval (Data), so the land holds `WLD-31`'s eleven biomes.
   Cover is the biome's mature shares regrown by α05's curves (`kd-life/src/plants/cover.rs`) from a last disturbance `since` drawn from the biome's fire and flood interval, with `tree_age` following, so the world starts with woods of mixed ages (A5.7, A7.4).
   `kd-world` cannot name `kd-life` (siblings, A2.3), so `gen::generate` gains a last argument, `life: &dyn GenLife`, a trait declared in `kd-world/src/gen/mod.rs` (`regrown_cover` here; α22a adds `place_herds`, α27a `rough_habitats` and `food_by_season`), which `kd-sim` implements over `kd-life` (`kd_sim::GenLifeImpl`) and `kd-app`'s `gen_job.rs`, `kd world new` and α19c's import pass in (A2.3 rule 1); a call that stops before step 10, as α18a's and α18b's tests do, passes `NoLife`.
   Species mixes are drawn when read (α02d's `plants::mix`, A5.2), only from species whose needs a cell meets; until α21 those are the island's thirteen (α02d's twelve and α10b's `bryony`), so cells none suits draw none.
6. `T18c.6` **Layers on the map and the cell card (`PRE-29`, `WLD-16`, `WLD-14`, A11.5).** `MapTexture`'s B channel becomes the cover class with forest density (A11.5); the world maker gains Biome, Warmth and Rain by season, Soil, and Deposits with a chip for each of flint, clay, ochre and copper, and its cell card gains "winter 4 °C, summer 19 °C, 820 mm, 4 storm days in autumn", the soil with its fertility, and the deposits; `kd world new` runs every step but herds and the start region; `kd map preview` gains `--layer biome|warmth:<season>|rain:<season>|soil|deposits:<kind>`.
7. `T18c.7` **Checks over many worlds and your look (`WLD-08`, `WLD-14`, `WLD-16`, `WLD-26`, A5.7).** `kd world check --climate --worlds 20` and `--deposits --worlds 100` print and test the numbers below; `tools/worldsheet.sh` renders the biome maps of seeds 1000–1019 onto one contact sheet, published with the note for your review (`WLD-08`'s "you review them"); the golden test takes the whole world at seed 1.
8. `T18c.8` **Timing and delivery (`WLD-11`, `PLT-09`, `PRC-11`, A5.7, A15.10, A14.9).** The world maker and `kd world new` report each step's time; the cloud bench records steps 0–10 at 1 km and 2 km; the phone benchmark (A15.10, α07d's `kd-app/src/bench.rs`) gains a "make one world" line, the first measure toward `WLD-11`'s three minutes (the full candidate run comes in α27a).
   `World::record_kinds()` gains `world.runoff`, with its `FINDABLE` line (the world maker's cell card; the place card's water line from α19a).
   New deposits, stones and biomes make this a big update: `major = 8`, `generator = 9`, earlier worlds opening read-only (`PLT-09`); fixture `a18c.kindling` (an island world with its climate records in their new place).
   Goldens `world-biomes-seed-1` and `world-rain-winter-seed-1`; `versionCode=4183`, `versionName=a18c`; `bench/cloud/a18c.json` adds steps 7–10 and the whole of one world at 1 km and 2 km; then P0's steps 5 to 8.

**Data:**
- `data/tuning/world.md`: `[climate]` (the warmth line's anchors, continentality 0.3, 0.6 and 1.0, lag a third of a season, 6 °C per 1,000 m, belts and their ±5° shift, moisture gain, drop 0.1 and 1.5 per 100 m, belt factors, record spreads 2.5, the worst year's factors from α13's `[weather]`), `[soils]`, `[deposits]` (the rates above, gravel × 0.8 per 10 km), `[biomes]` (the order and thresholds above).
- `data/world/biomes.md`: the eight new biomes with mature cover as trees, bushes, grass and herbs, reeds, bare (tropical forest 0.85, 0.08, 0.05, 0, 0.02; conifer forest 0.70, 0.10, 0.15, 0, 0.05; savanna 0.15, 0.10, 0.65, 0, 0.10; dry scrub 0.10, 0.45, 0.25, 0, 0.20; desert 0.01, 0.06, 0.08, 0, 0.85; tundra 0, 0.20, 0.55, 0, 0.25; mountain heights 0.02, 0.10, 0.45, 0, 0.43; ice 0, 0, 0, 0, 1), α02a's keeping theirs; fire and flood intervals in game years for all (grassland and savanna 3, dry scrub 15, marsh 50, conifer 60, tundra and mountain heights 100, broadleaf 150, tropical forest 400, desert, shore and ice none).
- `data/world/deposits.md`: `chert_in_limestone`, `obsidian`, `hard_stone`, `clay`, `ochre`, `copper_ore`, `native_copper`; `data/world/rocks.md`: `basalt` and `glassy_lava` name their loose items; `data/items/stone.md`: `basalt_cobble`, `obsidian_lump`.
- `data/VERSION.toml`: `major = 8`, `generator = 9`; `tests/golden/generator.toml`: the whole world at seed 1; `tests/fixtures/worlds/a18c.kindling`.

**Tests:**
- Unit, `crates/kd-world/tests/gen_climate.rs`: `rain_shadow_behind_a_ridge` (a test world with a 3,000 m north–south range across the westerlies: windward rain at least twice the lee's); `colder_6_degrees_per_km` (within each weather cell, warmth falls 6 ± 0.5 °C per 1,000 m); `seasons_reversed_between_halves` (northern summer is southern winter, `WLD-01`); `climate_record_round_trip`; `worst_year_on_every_generated_cell` (`GOD-05`); `calibration_matches_storm_days` (traced storm-hours after calibration within 10% of target, A5.8).
- Unit, `crates/kd-world/tests/gen_soils.rs`: `silt_on_floodplains`; `ash_near_volcanoes`; `peat_on_marshes`; `washed_out_where_hot_and_wet`; `biomes_reach_their_mature_cover` (each biome's shares within 5% once `since` passes its regrowth time).
- `kd world check --climate` (`WLD-16`'s Done when, first part; the weather's 20-year averages come in α20a): over 20 worlds, by 10° bands of latitude, tropical forest or savanna hold most land within 10° of the equator, desert or dry scrub at least 25% at 20–30°, broadleaf, conifer or grassland most at 40–60°, and tundra, conifer, mountain or ice most beyond 60°; and at 30–50°, coasts under warm currents are at least 2 °C warmer in winter than coasts at the same latitude under cold ones (`WLD-26`).
- `kd world check --deposits` (`WLD-14`'s Done when): over 100 worlds, flint only in chalk, some limestone (as chert) and gravel below them; obsidian only within 20 km of sticky volcanoes; copper ore only in volcanic lines within 50 km of granite.
- Catalogue: `basalt_cobble` and `obsidian_lump` complete (`MAT-17`); every deposit and rock names only items that exist.
- Golden: the whole world at seed 1; fixture `a18c.kindling` opens and runs a game day, and `a18b.kindling` opens read-only with its book (`PLT-09`).
- Bench: steps 0–10 at 1 km within 6 s on a cloud core and 1.5 s at 2 km; the phone's "make one world" line recorded.
- Your review: the 20-world contact sheet.

**On the phone:**
1. Open the alpha link; in Settings long-press the version line, tap World maker, then New with seed 1.
2. The map is now in biome colours: tropical greens round the middle, deserts in the dry belts, grassland, forests, tundra, and the ice.
3. Turn on Rain, first for winter, then summer: a range has a wet windward side and a dry lee.
4. Turn on Deposits → Flint: dots sit on chalk and down the rivers below it; then Copper: a few dots in volcanic ranges.
5. Tap a cell: "winter 4 °C, summer 19 °C, 820 mm; loam, fertility 3; flint in the river gravel".
6. Open the contact sheet of 20 worlds linked in the note and reply with anything that looks wrong.

**Not in this alpha:** weather that follows this climate hour by hour (α20a); plant species beyond the island's (α21); herds (α22a); the start region and the best three worlds (α27a).

**Risks:** climate belts too regular, giving stripes of biome: the moisture march and continentality break them up, judged on the contact sheet; a calibration that oscillates: capped at 8 rounds, with A5.8's fallback; too few chalk districts for flint in some worlds: α27a's must-haves reject those worlds, and the rate is tuned so at least 1 world in 4 qualifies (`WLD-10`).

### α19a Areas and walks everywhere (about 5.5 hours)

**Goal:** people live on a generated world: three or four bands start in a temperate window found on its land, every area anywhere is made from its world cell with its rivers, cliffs, caves, coasts and ice, and walks cross the whole world by its cells, wading and swimming rivers and climbing through cliff gaps.

**Serves:** `WLD-12` (part: areas made anywhere from their cells), `WLD-13` (part: unvisited places made from the seed), `WLD-34` (the generator fills the same values: cut presets and their check), `WLD-01` (part: a walk due east comes back from the west; the seam never crossed), `MAT-08` (part: worn paths everywhere), `BIO-21` (part: wading, swimming and climbing), `PRE-44` (part: wade, swim and climb), `WLD-24` (part: a stand-in start region), `BIO-03` (part: the start's bands on generated land), `PRE-35` (part: the place card on generated land), `PRE-13` (part: generated cells findable), `RES-18` (part: scenes on whole generated worlds, choosing only the start), `PLT-09` (part: a big update, marked).

**Architecture:** `A5.3`, `A5.5`, `A5.6`, `A5.12`, `A3.6`, `A3.7`, `A8.3`, `A8.8`, `A11.8`, `A12.4`, `A15.7`, `A14.9`.

**Needs:** α18c, with α02b's skeleton and ground, α02c's pieces and cave chambers, α02d's and α08's contents, α03d's ways and path cache, α06a's `first_band` and α12's 3–4 bands (`kd-people/src/setup.rs`), α09b's `fall()`, α13's hourly weather and α03a's mean-cycle weather (`kd_world::weather::preset`), α04d's place card and α07b's Worlds list.

**Crates and files touched:** `kd-world` (α02b's `src/area/skeleton.rs` and `src/area/ground.rs`, α02c's `src/area/pieces.rs`, α02d's `src/area/contents.rs`, α02a's `src/lands.rs`: cut presets, α03d's `src/path/cells.rs`, `src/path/blocks.rs` new, `src/gen/start_stub.rs` new, α13's `src/weather/hourly.rs`: the active window), `kd-data` (kind `Land`: `form = "cells"`), `kd-sim` (α03d's `src/paths.rs`, `src/world.rs`: `World::from_generated`, `src/scene.rs`: the `generated` key), `kd-people` (α12's `src/setup.rs`: bands at given shelters; α03c's `src/body/walk.rs`: wading, swimming and climbing), `kd-app` (the new-world job), `kd-ui` (α07b's `src/views/worlds.rs`, α04d's `src/views/place.rs`, `src/findable.rs`), `kd-render` (wade, swim and climb poses), `kd-tools` (`src/world.rs`: `kd world cut`), `data/models/movements.md`, `data/models/surfaces.md`, `data/tuning/world.md`, `data/VERSION.toml`, `tests/golden/generator.toml`, `scenes/lands/`, `scenes/`.

**Tasks:**
1. `T19a.1` **Areas from any generated cell (`WLD-12`, `WLD-13`, `PRE-35`, A5.3, A5.5).** α02b's skeleton and ground, α02c's pieces and α02d's and α08's contents read every generated layer: river cells' fixed entry and exit points joined by α02b's keyed meander and stream crossings toward `flow`, as on the island; lake shores at the lake's level from α18b's lake table; sea shores by shore kind (beach sand, rock platforms, estuary mud, salt-marsh reeds); escarpments from each cell's `cliff` (direction and height), α02b's single island line generalised: each cliff cell's line keyed on its own place uid and meeting its neighbours' at shared edge points, with α02b's gap at its lowest point; caves and lava tubes from α18b's cave records (α02c's 2–6 chambers by size class, a tube one long chamber); springs; exposures of the second layer where `exposed`; marsh (wet ground, reeds); and ice (the `ice` surface, no contents).
   Ground materials come from the 12 rocks' ladders and α18c's soils; stone patches from α18c's deposits by α08's rules; `data/models/surfaces.md` gains `ice` and `salt_mud`; lakes are drawn as α02b draws the island's sea, a flat surface at the lake's generated level, until α20c's water grid.
   Areas across the east–west wrap take their neighbours through `wrap` (A3.7), so an area at x = 0 meets the one at the far eastern edge exactly; nothing reads the camera (`WLD-13`).
   α04d's place card (`views/place.rs`) shows a generated cell's land: its rock layers, geology and any fault or volcano, its waters (stretch, lake, spring), soil and fertility, deposits showing, biome and the season's climate (`PRE-35`), the view α18a–α18c's `FINDABLE` lines name.
2. `T19a.2` **Cut presets (`WLD-34`, A5.6, A3.6).** `kd world cut <dir> <x0,y0,w,h> --out scenes/lands/<name>.toml` (A2.7's form, the window in cells) writes a scene land with `form = "cells"` (A5.6; α02a's kind `Land` gains it): its source's seed, generator version and place, every cell's fixed values and the window's climate records; `lands::build` reads it back into the same cells at the same place uids, and a scene names it as `land = "<name>"`.
   A cut compiled into the blob (by a demo, bench or review scene) stores its cells zstd-compressed; the blob's size is measured against A3.6's 1 MB line and flagged in the note.
   So a region set by hand and the same values from a generated world make identical areas: at least 2 cells inside a cut window, an area's hash equals the source world's (`WLD-34`'s Done when, first part).
   This alpha cuts `scenes/lands/cut-temperate-river.toml` from seed 1 (a 60 × 60 km window with a river, a limestone escarpment and caves; if seed 1 has none, the first seed from 1 up that has) for its scenes.
3. `T19a.3` **Walks across the world (`WLD-01`, `WLD-12`, `MAT-08`, A5.12, A3.7).** α03d's ways grow to A5.12's whole world: its cell search (`path/cells.rs`: A* on the 8-neighbour grid with Tobler's rule, cover, worn edges and fords) wraps east–west through `wrap` (A3.7), closes the sea, deep lakes and the seam rows, passes an escarpment step over 3 m only at the skeleton's gaps, slows in snow (α13), ties going to the lower cell index, and opens ice that bears once α20a gives it.
   Its landmass labels cover every generated cell (a flood fill over passable cells, rebuilt when fords or ice change), refusing unreachable ends at once, with the 100,000-expansion cap kept; a trip over 50 km is planned first on the 8 km block grid (A3.7 level 13, `path/blocks.rs`), then each block leg is refined, the step α03d left for whole worlds.
   α03d's cache (`kd-sim/src/paths.rs`) keeps its keys, its version rule and its 65,536 ways for the whole world; clusters read it in a window and add ways at the barrier in cluster order (A5.12).
   α03d's worn paths (`worn`) wear and fade on every generated cell (`MAT-08`), drawn through their cells' keyed path points.
4. `T19a.4` **Wading, swimming and climbing (`BIO-21`, `PRE-44`, `BIO-14`, `BIO-13`, A8.3, A11.8).** A crossing of a stream or river cell is a ford where the water is at most waist deep (1 m for adults, 0.6 m for children) and depth × speed is at most α03d's `ford_limit` (0.5 m²/s); it is wadeable, the walker's pace halved.
   Where the river is deeper but slower than 0.5 m/s and narrower than 30 m, adults whose stamina is at least 0.6 of the average may swim it: A8.3's breath falls 10 a minute while swimming (tuned), chill rises in water under 10 °C, and a swimmer whose breath reaches 0 sinks and drowns after 3 minutes under (`BIO-14`, α06c's `Death`); children, the old and the weak never take such a crossing, and anything wider or faster is closed.
   Escarpment gaps and steps of 1.5–3 m are climbed at a quarter pace, with a slip at 1 in 2,000 climbs, a fall through α09b's `fall()` (`BIO-13`, tuned).
   `data/models/movements.md` gains `wade`, `swim` and `climb` (4 key poses each, A11.8's closed list), each with step marks for sound (A13.5), switched on by the path segment's kind (`PRE-44`).
5. `T19a.5` **A stand-in start on generated land (`WLD-24`, `BIO-03`, A5.7, A8.8).** `gen/start_stub.rs`: `start_stub(w: &GenWorld) -> Option<StartStub>` scans windows of 40 × 40 cells every 10 cells over land in row order from a keyed offset, and returns the first whose coldest-season mean is 2–10 °C with at least 3 dry caves or shelters of size class 1 or more, at least 5 km apart, each with a river, spring-fed stream or lake within 2 km, and flint or chert (in chalk, limestone or gravel) within 10 km of one of them; it gives the window, its 3–4 shelters and their home ranges (cells within 10 km) and marks the world header "stand-in start" (`WLD-24` in part; α27a grows it into A5.7's ranking).
   `kd-sim/src/world.rs`: `World::from_generated(gen: &GenWorld, stub: &StartStub, cat: &Catalogue) -> World`, beside α03a's `World::from_land`, makes the bands with α12's set-up (`kd-people/src/setup.rs`, α06a's `first_band` once a band, 3–4 bands of 15–30, `BIO-03`) at those shelters, with A8.8's starting knowledge read from the generated cells, one band holding a fire (`BIO-02`).
   Until the world-wide layers arrive, an active window, the start window and 100 km round it, runs as the island does: α13's hourly weather on the generated climate records there, every other weather cell on α03a's mean daily and seasonal cycle (`kd_world::weather::preset`, A5.6's pre-weather mode) until α20a; rivers at their rated mean levels, as the island's, until α20c's routing; α05's cover step and seasons on the window's cells until α21; and herds and small game placed round the start window at the island preset's numbers (red deer 300, wild boar 120, wolves 15; small game at its densities) until α22a places them everywhere.
6. `T19a.6` **New generated world (test) and the `generated` scene key (`WLD-12`, `RES-18`, A15.7, A12.4).** α07b's Worlds list gains "New generated world (test)": a seed field (random by default), α18c's generation with its progress line, the stand-in start, and the world opening at camp zoom at the first band's shelter; a seed whose stub finds no window says so ("no start region in this world"); the first-launch screen stays the first region until α27a.
   Scene settings gain `generated = { seed }` (an addition to A15.7, written into the architecture in this branch): the whole world of that seed with its stand-in start, which the phone's Make test world generates in about 20 s before running; it chooses only the start (`RES-18`).
7. `T19a.7` **Scenes, the demo world and delivery (`WLD-12`, `BIO-21`, `PLT-09`, `PRC-11`, A14.9).** Write and run the scenes under Tests; `a19a-generated-band-year` is the demo.
   Areas made from every generated layer change area-making: a big update, `major = 9`, `generator = 10`, the golden areas re-blessed and 20 areas of seed 1 added to `tests/golden/generator.toml`, earlier worlds opening read-only (`PLT-09`); no chunk changes its schema (cut lands are scene data), so no fixture is added.
   Goldens `generated-camp`, `generated-cliff-gap` and `generated-wade`; `versionCode=4191`, `versionName=a19a`; `bench/cloud/a19a.json` adds an area by a generated cliff (A5.5), world ways against A5.12's 100 µs average with the cache, a whole generated world of about 100 people saved and opened by α07a's full saves (for α19c to beat), and the blob's size; then P0's steps 5 to 8.
