### α48 Specialists, chiefs and priests (about 4.5 hours)

**Goal:** people known for a craft work for others for gifts, and in villages with full stores some do it full time; heads of families decide together in village councils; in a large village a leader of ten years becomes chief for life, setting the plans, ruling on feuds and punishing, and the shaman becomes a priest fed by gifts, holding the calendar's rites in a house by the sacred place.

**Serves:** `CUL-32`, `CUL-22` (part: councils in villages; chiefs), `CUL-26` (part: priests), `CUL-06` (part: the chief punishes, death for a killing), `CUL-08` (part: a chief's death sentence, told plainly), `CUL-31` (part: the chief rules on feuds), `CUL-33` (part: the first chief; its early side read nightly), `MND-33` (part: work asked of a specialist, paid with a gift), `MND-13` (part: specialists teach for gifts), `CUL-29` (part: calendar rites held by priests), `CUL-34` (part: the priest leads rites), `MND-32` (part: the ambition `lead` reached as chief), `CUL-07` (part: roles as facts people act on), `PRE-35` (part: roles on cards), `PRE-39` (part: chiefs and priests recognised), `PRE-17` (part: the death sentence's trap record), `PRE-13` (part: specialists, chiefs and priests findable).

**Architecture:** `A9.7`, `A9.8`, `A9.11`, `A9.1`, `A9.5`, `A9.6`, `A9.9`, `A9.15`, `A9.16`, `A8.15`, `A8.18`, `A8.19`, `A10.7`, `A12.4`, `A12.5`, `A12.6`, `A12.7`, `A12.8`, `A14.8`, `A14.9`, `A15.7`.

**Needs:** α47b, with α46a's villages (`kd-culture/src/villages.rs`, the `large` flag), α26b's leaders and roles (`kd-culture/src/roles.rs`, `cul.leaders`, `data/culture/plans.md`), α30a's `ask_to_make` and `give_gift`, α32a's punishments and question 8 (`kd-culture/src/customs.rs`), α32b's shamans and sacred places (`roles.rs`, `religion.rs`, `cul.shamans`) and its moment `role_holder_died`, α39a's feuds (`end_feud(feud, Ruling)`), α40's councils and calendar (`kd-culture/src/council.rs`, `council_held`, `council_ruled`, `Occasion::Calendar(sign)`), α12's teaching, α29's ambition `lead`, α30b's `data/text/deaths.md` and α35a's trap set.

**Crates and files touched:** `kd-culture` (`src/specialists.rs` new; α26b's `src/roles.rs`: chiefs and priests; α40's `src/council.rs`: village councils; α32a's punishments; α32b's `src/religion.rs`: the rite house; the yearly batch), `kd-people` (α30a's `ask_to_make`; α04c's `src/choose/options.rs`: `gift_to_priest`, `settle_a_feud`), `kd-sim` (`src/scene.rs`: `roles`), `kd-player` (α11b's `src/book/`), `kd-save` (the `cul.groups` migration), `kd-text` (the plain death sentence), `kd-ui` (α12's band and village card, α04d's person card, α12's craft card, `src/findable.rs`), `data/culture/plans.md`, `data/minds/thoughts.md`, `data/text/culture.md`, `data/text/deaths.md`, `data/writer/traps.md`, `data/history/event_kinds.md`, `data/tuning/culture.md`, `tools/nightly.sh`, `tests/fixtures/worlds/`, `scenes/`.

**Tasks:**
1. `T48.1` **Specialists (`CUL-32`, `MND-33`, `MND-13`, `PRE-13`, A9.8, A9.5, A8.19).** α30a's `ask_to_make` grows: the asker gives a gift worth at least the work's hours × `[roles] gift_per_hour` (a twelfth of a day's food, tuned), food or a thing, by α30a's `give_gift`, and the maker gets the option to make it and hand it over (`MND-33`).
   `crates/kd-culture/src/specialists.rs` (new): each person keeps `for_others: [u8; 60]`, a ring over the last game year of 60 days (`TIM-18`): the sector they spent 2 hours or more on that day making things for someone outside their family who paid a gift, or 0; kept in `Culture`'s per-person role columns, chunk `cul.groups`, as A9 keeps roles (A9, A14.3).
   The yearly batch (A9.8) names, for each sector, the member with most such days in the ring, at least 6 (`[roles] specialist_min_days`, tuned), ties to higher sector experience then lower uid, as the band's specialist; a people's first in a sector logs `specialist_named`.
   Asks go to them first: an `ask_to_make` toward a sector's specialist scores +5 (`[roles] ask_bonus`, A8.15) above others who know the blueprint; they teach for a gift as reason enough (A8.19), taking apprentices aged 10–16 from their band before others (A9.5, `MND-13`).
   Full time has no rule of its own: when gifts fill most of a family's food, its stores meet the specialist's hunger and craft work wins their choosing (A8.15), so "works most days at one craft, fed by others" is measured, never set.
   `World::record_kinds()` gains `cul.specialists`, with its `FINDABLE` line (the person card's role line and the craft card).
2. `T48.2` **Councils in villages (`CUL-22`, `MND-09`, A9.7).** α40's `kd-culture/src/council.rs` (councils at gatherings) gains villages, with no second council module: in a village without a chief, a head of family who would set a group plan of A9.7's list proposes it instead, at most once a day a village; at the next dusk the heads present meet for an hour (a shared activity of 3 heads or more).
   Each head backs, by their own choosing (`MND-09`), the proposal they score best, or none; the proposal whose backers' respect, as the other heads hold it, sums highest becomes the council's plan, set and told like any group plan, logging α40's `council_held`; a village council punishes through α40's rulings, writing question 9's case "the council" (`council_ruled`), as at gatherings.
3. `T48.3` **Chiefs (`CUL-22`, `CUL-31`, `CUL-06`, `CUL-08`, `MND-32`, `PRE-17`, A9.7, A9.6, A9.9, A12.7, A12.8).** In α26b's `kd-culture/src/roles.rs`: in a large village (α46a's flag), a leader who has led for 10 game years becomes chief for life (role `chief`, A9.7's seventh role list); α26b's leader record (record kind `cul.leaders`, chunk `cul.groups`) gains `chief_since`, with its migration; `chief_made` is logged (kept forever, first-able).
   Only the chief sets group plans (A9.7's table), the village council stops, and any adult may set `defend` while the chief is more than 2 km away.
   Feuds (A9.9): an open feud among the village's families gives the chief the option `settle_a_feud`, a ruling chosen like any option: gifts from the wrongdoer's family that the victim's kin value above revenge, a marriage between the families, or driving the wrongdoer out; it ends the feud through α39a's `end_feud(feud, Ruling)` and logs `chief_ruled`.
   Punishing (A9.6): the chief is the punisher whatever question 9's answer says, choosing among α32a's punishments, and for a killing within the band the one α32a left to chiefs, death; it is dark-tagged by `CUL-08`'s list, logs `punished_with_death` (kept forever; dark: killing), and is told by its own plain pattern in α30b's `data/text/deaths.md` that never goes to the writer (`PRE-17`, A12.8); α35a's `data/writer/traps.md` gains its `TrapRecord`, with planted rewordings the checks must reject (A12.7).
   At the chief's death question 8's answer picks the next leader (α32a), who becomes chief after 10 years of their own; a chief stays one for life if the village shrinks, and the role ends if the band leaves its village; becoming chief reaches the ambition `lead` (α29's `ambition_reached`, `MND-32`).
4. `T48.4` **Priests (`CUL-26`, `CUL-29`, `CUL-34`, A9.11).** In a large village with a shaman (α32b's role), the shaman becomes its priest at the next yearly batch (role `priest`); α32b's shaman record (record kind `cul.shamans`, chunk `cul.groups`) gains `priest_since` and `rite_house`, with its migration; `priest_made` is logged (kept forever, first-able).
   After a rite the priest led, or a healing they gave, each joiner, or the healed person's family, gets the option `gift_to_priest` (food or a thing, α30a's `give_gift`), scored by belief in the rite's spirit (`MND-31`), favours owed (`MND-26`) and kindness; the priest's family eats from these gifts as a specialist's does (A9.8).
   The house: a lasting house within 200 m of the band's sacred place (α32b's `religion.rs`) with nobody sleeping in it is set aside as the `rite_house`; if there is none, the priest sets α26b's `build_together` for one there (A9.7, T46a.3).
   α40's calendar rites already come due on their signs (`Occasion::Calendar(sign)`): with a priest, they and the band's kept rites are held at the `rite_house`, the priest leading.
   At the priest's death the successor is whoever joined most of their rites in the last 5 game years, the priest's child first on ties, else α32b's shaman rule (`CUL-26`).
5. `T48.5` **Roles on cards and in the book (`PRE-35`, `PRE-39`, `CUL-33`, `RES-07`, A12.4, A12.5, A12.6, A10.7, A14.8).** The band and village cards (A12.4) list the chief and since when, the priest, the council's heads and the specialists by sector; α04d's person card gains a role line ("Chief of Alder Bend since Year 241", "Specialist in pottery · worked for others 34 of the last 60 days"); α12's craft card names each band's specialist.
   α07b's table gains `specialist_named` (first-able), `chief_made`, `chief_ruled` (logged), `priest_made` and `punished_with_death`; α26b's `data/text/culture.md` gains `specialist_named`, `chief_made`, `chief_ruled`, `priest_made`, 5 phrasings and a short form each.
   α11b's recognisers: `chief_made`, `priest_made` and `specialist_named` are a people's firsts, a chief's as a leader entry; the world's first `chief_made` is read for `CUL-33`'s window (A9.16); α32b's `role_holder_died` moment covers a chief's or priest's death (A10.7).
   α12's `tools/nightly.sh` reads each pace world's first `chief_made` against the early side of `CUL-33`'s window 150–350, one before Year 60 counting against it.
6. `T48.6` **Scenes, the demo world and delivery (`CUL-22`, `CUL-32`, `PRC-11`, A15.7, A14.9).** Bands gain the start key `roles = { leader_years, shaman, chief }` (how long the leader has led, who holds the shaman's role, a chief already made), an addition to A15.7 choosing only the start (`RES-18`), written into the architecture in this branch.
   Write and run the scenes under Tests; `a48-chief` is the demo.
   The specialists' rings, α26b's leader record and α32b's shaman role, all in `cul.groups`, bring its migration and fixture `a48.kindling` (A14.9).
   Goldens `village-card-roles` and `person-card-chief`; `versionCode=7480`, `versionName=a48`; `bench/cloud/a48.json` adds the specialists' ring and the village councils (within A9.17's culture costs) and the 1 line; then P0's steps 5 to 8.

### α49 Catalogue I: crafts (about 5.5 hours)

**Goal:** every craft sector of `MAT-23` reaches exactly its launch count, each new blueprint with its made item, model, sound, trials and scene, checked batch by batch, so a workshop test world shows the full range of tools, foods, traps and gear.

**Serves:** `MAT-23` (part: stone, wood, fire, cooking, hunting, gathering and healing filled to their counts), `MAT-10` (part: the made items they make), `MAT-16`, `MAT-17` (part: every check on each batch), `MAT-14`, `MAT-21` (part: names, icons and models of the new results), `MAT-07` (part: second routes to known results), `MND-11` (part: each new blueprint discoverable), `PRE-46` (part: their layouts), `PRE-42` (part: made things drawn from their materials), `SND-06` (part: their sound blueprints), `RES-23` (part: a scene for each new blueprint), `RES-24` (part: their trials), `RSK-25` (part: the craft fallback set).

**Architecture:** `A6.15`, `A6.14`, `A6.7`, `A6.2`, `A6.3`, `A6.12`, `A3.6`, `A11.7`, `A13.5`, `A15.7`.

**Needs:** α48 (the stage's own blueprints are in: herding α44, farming and cooking α45, building α46a, fire and pottery α47a, metal α47b), with α08's and α09's catalogues and tools (`kd catalog build --assign`, `check`, `pairs`, `trials`, `tables`, `kd scene gen`).

**Crates and files touched:** `kd-tools` (`kd catalog count` new), `kd-data` (the launch check), `data/launch.toml` new, `data/blueprints/stone.md`, `wood.md`, `fire.md`, `cooking.md`, `hunting.md`, `gathering.md`, `healing.md`, `data/items/*.md`, `data/states.md`, `data/models/layouts.md`, `data/sounds/blueprints.md`, `tools/catalog-checklist.md` new, `scenes/gen/`, `results/catalog/`, `scenes/`.

**Tasks:**
1. `T49.1` **Launch counts and the count tool (`MAT-23`, `MAT-10`, `RSK-25`, A3.6, A6.15).** `data/launch.toml` (new, check-only: read by `kd catalog count` and `kd catalog check --launch`, never by a rule) holds the launch targets: items about 190 (about 90 raw, about 100 made, `MAT-10`); blueprints by sector exactly (stone 14, wood 13, fire 10, cooking 14, hunting 10, gathering 7, hides 16, building 12, healing 7, pottery 7, herding 4, farming 6, metal 5, art 8, music 3, `MAT-23`); plants about 60 (`WLD-31`); wild animals about 30 and domestic kinds 5 (`WLD-32`); illnesses 15 (`BIO-05`); thoughts about 100 (`MND-29`); kinds of event with patterns about 100 (`PRE-37`).
   Tolerances: "about" totals within 10%; sector counts, domestic kinds and illnesses exact; the core targets of `RSK-25` (about 125 items, 95 blueprints, 40 plants, 20 wild animals, 10 illnesses); a `[[reason]]` line for any count outside its tolerance, naming the alpha and why, for the owner to read in the stage report.
   `kd catalog count [--biomes] [--core]` prints present against target by catalogue, class and sector (and by biome, T50.1) into `results/catalog/count.json`; `--launch` fails outside tolerance without a reason line, the gate α51 turns on.
2. `T49.2` **What each sector still lacks (`MAT-23`, `MAT-16`, A6.15).** `kd catalog count` before the first batch must show stone 5, wood 6, fire 8, cooking 8, hunting 8, gathering 4, hides 16, building 12, healing 6, pottery 7, herding 4, farming 6, metal 5, art 8, music 3; any other figure is reconciled with the earlier stages' notes before a batch starts.
   A candidate counts as present when an entry with the same action and the same named result or state exists, whatever its id; each sector adds its candidates in order until it reaches its count, never past it, a spare after the count being taken only when a candidate above it is found present.
   These are already in the catalogue under the ids given and are never added again: stone `chopper_by_striking` (α09's), `blade_by_striking` (α24b's `strike_a_blade`); wood `wooden_spear_by_scraping` (α23's `point_a_stick`), `point_by_hardening` (α23's `harden_a_point`), `digging_stick_by_scraping` (α09's `point_by_scraping`); 6. `T49.6` **How each batch is checked (`MAT-17`, `MAT-14`, `RES-23`, `RES-24`, `PRE-46`, A6.15, A6.14, A15.7).** After each batch, in order, until clean (A6.15): `kd catalog build --assign` (new ids into `data/ids.lock`); `kd catalog check` (complete, reachable, discoverable with each new blueprint's first route listed, possible, expected fits, mass, reality rules); `kd catalog pairs` (each new fit named in `fits` or `meant`, or with a reason, else the ranges narrowed, `RSK-06`); `kd catalog trials` (200 tries at levels 1 and 8, `RES-24`); `kd catalog tables`; `kd catalog count`, each sector at or under its count.
   α09's `kd scene gen` writes each new blueprint's scene in `scenes/gen/` (someone who knows it, inputs in reach from items its ranges fit, decoys beside them, `RES-23`), each with `base_seed = 49200` plus 10 × its place in this alpha's list, run by `kd scene run --quick`, passing when its result is made in at least 10 of 20 runs within a game day.
   `data/sounds/blueprints.md` gains each new pair of action and sounding class its sound blueprint, or a silent mark (A13.5); motifs need no entry, since α33's `kd-render/src/art.rs` draws them from the models.
   A reviewer agent in a separate session reads each batch's diff against `tools/catalog-checklist.md` (new: the main characteristic fits the use; tools wear by their role; bindings need fibre 3 or more or stickiness 4 or more, `RCK-25`; foods name their source's group; no value in the wrong field; sizes and times plausible and in their units; no candidate present under another id) and records its verdict in the pull request; findings are fixed before the next batch.

   Write and run the scenes under Tests; `a49-workshop` is the demo.
   No chunk schema changes; a small update (new made items and blueprints only).
   Goldens `workshop-sheet` (the new made items on pedestals in two materials) and `thing-card-new`; `versionCode=7490`, `versionName=a49`; `bench/cloud/a49.json` with the 1 line; the note lists what each batch added, sector by sector; then P0's steps 5 to 8.

**Tests:**

- `kd catalog check` (with `--core`), `pairs`, `trials`, `tables` and `count` clean after every batch, every sector at or under its count and the seven filled sectors exactly at it; every new blueprint's generated scene passes at 10 of 20.

**On the phone:**
1. Open the alpha link; in Settings long-press the version line, tap Make test world and pick `a49 · Workshop`, then open it from Worlds (day 5).
2. Pinch to close camp: people at many crafts at once, grinding an axe, weaving baskets, knotting a net, rendering fat, scraping bowls.
3. Tap five made things: each card names its materials, maker and quality, and each looks like what it is made of.
4. Open the book of ages: the discoveries named over the five days, each with its people's word.

**Not in this alpha:** plants, wild animals and raw materials (α50); the launch gate and the lists' checks (α51); hides, building, pottery, art and music, full before this alpha.

**Risks:** earlier stages named entries differently from these candidates, so a craft could be added twice: presence is judged by action and result, never by id, the drop list above is checked first, and the reviewer checks each batch for doubles; a sector running past its count: `kd catalog count` runs after every batch and fails it; a new entry fitting blueprints it shouldn't (a bark axe): `kd catalog pairs` lists every new fit and none passes unnamed (`RSK-06`); the batches running long: each is at most 15 entries, about an hour (A6.15), and an unfinished batch moves whole to α51 with a note.

### α50 Catalogue II: the land (about 5.5 hours)

**Goal:** the world reaches its launch plants and wild animals, every land biome with at least 6 plants and 4 animals and seas and shores with 4 animals, every kind of land with a grazer, a hunter, a food plant and a fibre plant, each with its yields, model, call and bestiary card, the wild sheep among them; new worlds show them.

**Serves:** `WLD-31` (part: about 60 species, 6 a biome), `WLD-32` (part: about 30 wild species, 4 a biome; the wild sheep, the last wild kin of a domestic kind), `MAT-10` (part: raw items to about 90), `WLD-18` (part: the world without people run again), `WLD-10` (part: the must-haves over the full lists), `MND-21` (part: the snake half of its Done when), `PRE-16` (part: their cards), `PRE-46` (part: plant forms and body patterns), `SND-06` (part: their calls), `SND-11` (part: birdsong where small birds live), `MAT-16`, `MAT-17` (part: every check on each batch), `RSK-25` (part: plants, wild animals and raw items in the fallback set), `PLT-09` (part: a big update, marked).

**Architecture:** `A7.2`, `A7.6`, `A7.12`, `A5.7`, `A5.13`, `A6.2`, `A6.15`, `A3.6`, `A14.9`, `A11.7`, `A11.3`, `A13.5`, `A12.4`, `A15.7`, `A15.8`.

**Needs:** α49, with α21's plants and α22a's animals (`data/plants/`, `data/animals/wild.md`, `data/models/plants.md`, `data/models/animals.md`), α18c's `GenLife` (`regrown_cover`, `place_herds`, `rough_habitats`, `food_by_season`) and `kd-world/src/plants.rs`'s species mix, α16c's recordings, α22b's bestiary, α27a's must-haves and α28's ready fears (`a28-ready-fears`, `[ready_fears]`).

**Crates and files touched:** `kd-tools` (`kd catalog count --biomes`), `kd-world` (A5.7's habitat and biome tables through α18c's `GenLife`; `src/plants.rs`'s mix), `kd-life` (habitats), `data/plants/`, `data/animals/wild.md`, `data/items/` (raw), `data/models/plants.md`, `data/models/animals.md`, `data/palette/`, `data/sounds/recordings.md`, `assets/sounds/`, `assets/LICENSES.md`, `data/VERSION.toml`, `tests/golden/generator.toml`, `tests/fixtures/worlds/`, `scenes/`.

**Tasks:**
1. `T50.1` **Inventory by biome and kind of land (`WLD-31`, `WLD-32`, `RSK-25`).** `kd catalog count --biomes` lists, for each land biome of `WLD-31` but ice (tundra, northern conifer forest, broadleaf forest, grassland, dry scrub, desert, savanna, tropical forest, marsh, mountain heights) the plants and animals whose `biomes` or `habitat` include it, and the animals of seas and shores, against 6 plants and 4 animals (4 animals for seas and shores); and for each land biome whether it has a grazer, a hunter, a food plant and a fibre plant.
   The batches below add, in this order of need: biomes under their minimum; kinds of land missing a grazer, hunter, food plant or fibre plant; then the rest of each list in order until plants reach about 60 and wild animals about 30 (`data/launch.toml`), the count at the start being about 37 plants (α02d's 12, α10b's `bryony` and α21's) and 17 wild animals (α12b's 6 and α22a's 11).
   A candidate is present when an entry of the same species exists, whatever its id, and serves every biome it lists; these are already present and never added again: `acacia`, `alder`, `cloudberry`, `cotton_grass`, `date_palm`, `juniper`, `lime_tree`, `ramsons`, `wild_carrot`, `wild_fig`, `wild_olive`, `wild_yam`, `dwarf_willow` (for `arctic_willow`), `hoof_fungus`; `hare`, `wild_boar`, `wolf`, `wild_goat`, `aurochs` (for wild cattle), `reindeer`, `gazelle`, `brown_bear`, `lion`, `leopard`, `seal`, `salmon`, `sea_fish` (for cod), `mussel`, `red_deer`, `river_fish`, `small_birds`; and the raw items `bast`, `resin`, `palm_fronds`, `starchy_root` and `basalt_cobble`.

### α52 Pace (about 5 hours)

**Goal:** every step of the arc and every culture window lands in its years in typical worlds: the late steps are tuned in scenes set where each becomes possible, nightly runs confirm the early ones still hold, the full pace test of 10 worlds to Year 500 on fresh seeds, run over one or two nights, judges them all, and the world with everything runs at the stage's speed, with a page of charts you can open on the phone.

**Serves:** `TIM-19`, `RES-07`, `RES-16`, `CUL-33`, `PRN-17`, `RSK-26`, `RSK-01`, `RES-13` (part: 10 more worlds on a failure), `BIO-04` (part: Year 400), `BIO-06` (part: Year 500), `MAT-08` (part: an abandoned camp after 200 years), `PRE-09` (part: graves and old camps visitable), `MAT-07` (part: two routes to fire and huts), `PRE-39` (part: every age at a turning point), `CUL-07` (part: peoples of different spirits, customs and kinds of leader), `RES-25`, `RES-14`, `RES-12`, `PLT-10` (part: a Year-500 world's size), `PLT-04` (part: the stage's speed, old worlds and memory in the cloud), `TIM-07` (part: every row measured in the cloud), `MND-15` (part: about 2,000 people at half speed), `MND-14` (part: speed won without a cheaper mind), `WLD-04` (part: measured), `PLT-05` (part: runs that resume), `SCP-15` (part: the computing used), `RSK-14`, `VIS-03` (part: the arc from caves to copper).

**Architecture:** `A15.8`, `A15.7`, `A15.10`, `A15.14`, `A9.16`, `A12.5`, `A14.6`, `A14.10`, `A16.1`, `A16.3`, `A16.4`, `A16.5`, `A16.7`, `A8.21`, `A17.1`, `A17.8`.

**Needs:** α51 (the full catalogue), with α12's and α27b's pace runs (`tools/nightly.sh`, the tuning seeds in `data/TUNING-LOG.md`), α43c's Year-150 worlds, α43b's `kd bench --old` and speed work, α27b's generated bench worlds, α23b's `kd world cut`, α07a's saves and exports, α07e's `kd report` and the scenes whose first years each Stage 7 alpha recorded.

**Crates and files touched:** `kd-tools` (`kd world sample` new, `kd world seeds --fresh` new, `kd report --run`), `kd-sim`, `kd-people` and `kd-culture` (wherever T52.8's costs lie), `data/TUNING-LOG.md`, `data/tuning/*.md`, `data/blueprints/*.md` (discovery factors), `scenes/` (`a52-pace-*`, `a52-land-capacity`), `tests/oddities.toml`, `tests/ranges.toml`, `bench/budgets.toml`, `results/pace/`, `results/perf-a52.md`, the `runs` branch.

**Tasks:**
1. `T52.1` **Late-step scenes (`RES-16`, `TIM-19`, `CUL-33`, A15.7).** `scenes/a52-pace-*.toml` hold one scene per late target, each set where the step becomes possible (`RES-16`), run on the 20 tuning seeds of `data/TUNING-LOG.md`; their pass rules are records for tuning, never gates.
   `kd world sample --year N <worlds>` (new) writes the median knowledge of the nightly or Year-150 worlds at year N (blueprints held and skills by sector, customs, kept dogs) as a scene's `knowledge`, and α23b's `kd world cut` takes the land from such a world around a start region.
   The scenes, each until its stated limit: herding (3 bands, about 90 people, Year-100 knowledge, wild goats or boar in range; until 150 game years), villages (3 bands with Year-150 knowledge, sowing, herds or a salmon river; until 120), farming (3 bands with Year-60 knowledge that camp by wild grain each summer, with heaps; until 120), copper (a people of potters with Year-250 knowledge, kilns, charcoal and green ore within a day's walk; until 150) and the first chief (a large village under a new leader; until 60).
   From each scene's first-step times, censored runs counting their years, `kd report` estimates the yearly chance λ a band meeting the conditions takes the step; the expected first year in a whole world is the year the conditions first hold there (read from the nightly and Year-150 worlds) plus 1 ÷ (bands meeting them × λ).
   Tuning aims that median at each window's middle: herding about Year 185, villages 200, farming 275, copper 400, the first chief 250 (`TIM-19`, `CUL-33`); each scene stays within 2 session-hours a night (`RES-09`).
2. `T52.2` **Tuning, and only tuning (`RES-16`, `PRN-17`, `TIM-19`).** Only chances and amounts change, the same in every world: discovery factors (`sow_seed`, `plant_roots`, `pen_by_stacking`, `milk_by_pressing`, `pit_house_frame`, `post_house_frame`, `blown_firing`, `ore_by_grinding`, `copper_by_smelting`), the chance a surprise is noticed, how often people experiment, the dream-hint chance, `heap_per_kg`, taming rates (A7.11), `keep_animals`' second goal, `[villages] move_margin` and `large_from`, split sizes and the crowd start rate.
   Never a window, a pass rule, a number `PROJECT.md` states as a rule (five settled years, ten years as leader, heat 5, generation 5) or a date, and never past a floor a Check sets, such as a tended plot yielding at least twice an untended one (`RCK-23`); nothing is scripted (`PRN-17`).
   Each change is a line in `data/TUNING-LOG.md` with the value before and after, what it was tuned against (scene, measure, seeds) and the date; `python3 tools/filecheck.py file` fails if a pace-test seed appears there.
3. `T52.3` **Nightly confirmation (`RES-07`, `TIM-19`, `CUL-33`, `RES-25`).** After each tuning change the nightly set (20 worlds to Year 60, α12's `tools/nightly.sh`) runs on the tuning seeds and must keep every earlier target in its years (flakes, fire, clothing, huts, shared spirits, rites, myths, band splits, festivals), `RES-25`, and the early sides of every later window, this stage's five among them; once before the full test, α43c's Year-150 set runs on the tuning seeds for pottery, dogs, new peoples, feuds, raids' early side and Keeps going.
4. `T52.4` **The full pace test (`RES-07`, `TIM-19`, `PLT-05`, `RSK-14`, `SCP-15`, A15.8, A14.6).** 10 worlds to Year 500 on fresh seeds (`kd world seeds --fresh 10`, never in the tuning log), with no acts of yours (`TIM-19`): five cloud sessions side by side (A15.8), each running 2 worlds with 2 workers, detached; checkpoints are ordinary saves on disk every game year (A14.6); slim exports go every 3 real hours to `runs/pace-full-<date>/` on the `runs` branch when under 50 MB, with `status.json` and `results/` each night; each session wakes itself every 30 minutes to restart a stopped world from its newest checkpoint, ending identical (`PLT-05`, `RSK-14`).
   The owner's one-time OK for this computing (about 100–130 CPU-hours, 7–9 hours on five sessions, A15.8) is asked in α51's note, or this one's before starting, if not yet given (`RES-07`, `SCP-15`); no session creates a GitHub release or sets a commit status.

   Whole-world checks at their first size (`RES-07`): at least 8 of 10 hold 1,000–3,000 people at Year 400 (`BIO-04`); every inherited body number and trait within about 5% of the start at Year 500 (`BIO-06`); an abandoned cave camp's stone and fired clay remain, buried a few centimetres, after 200 years, its hides and wood gone (`MAT-08`); every grave and old camp listed can be visited, each find naming its maker and date (`PRE-09`); two routes each to fire and to huts (`MAT-07`); every age begins at a turning point (`PRE-39`); peoples end with different spirits, customs and kinds of leader (`CUL-07`); Keeps going in at least half the worlds (`CUL-33`); `RES-25`, `RES-14`'s ranges and `RES-12`'s oddities, each oddity a bug fixed with a test that would catch it again.
   Phone limits read in the cloud: each Year-500 world's present state, kept areas and history within about 4 GB (`PLT-10`), kept areas within about 1 GiB (`PLT-04`).

   A row below its target is won back as α43b did, largest excess first, with the same results more cheaply (A8.21), never smaller caps, a cheaper mind or rules that change with load (`MND-14`), each change proven by `kd det` (1 against 4 workers, serial against parallel, a save and reload mid-window: equal state hashes); a row still missed names its biggest cost in `results/perf-a52.md` for the stage report, with the plan to win it back (`PLT-04`, A16.1, A17.1).

### α53a Export and worlds across updates (about 4 hours)

**On the phone:**
1. Install this alpha's APK over α52's; open `a52 · Fed by the land` (in Settings long-press the version line and Make test world, if it is gone): it carries on, and its book shows "The rules changed: alpha a53a".

**Not in this alpha:** the stage close, settings polish, help cards and the release key (α53b).

every scene's result with its runs and range (`RES-13`), each beside its whole-world confirmation (`RES-21`); the sharp-stone test and its control (`RES-02`, `RES-03`); `MOM-08`'s and `MOM-12`'s scenes with their latest results and their appearances in the pace worlds, beside the earlier moments' (`RES-17`); the full test's windows and checks of T52.5 (`RES-07`); entries and live moments per game year (`RES-25`); births, deaths by cause, life spans and band and village sizes against `tests/ranges.toml` (`RES-14`); the trap set's cloud results and the phone's `KDT1:`; the phone's measurements against `PLT-04`'s targets and the stage budget of 1, met or missed, the costliest systems named if missed; the moments seen, the oddities flagged and any surprises (`RES-12`); each principle's Check (`PRN-16`) and what was added without rewriting anything earlier, or why (`PRN-14`); every kind of record the world keeps with the card or view showing it, from `FINDABLE` (`PRE-13`); the risks, with the content made against the launch counts and α51's reason lines (`RSK-25`); where every test ran and the computing used, the full test's CPU-hours among them (`SCP-15`), and the repository's size against A17.10's 3 GB line (if past it, unless an earlier report already asked, the owner's choice between adding their own GitHub token, so the APKs go to releases, and deleting old `runs` branches); `PLT-03`'s Done when, met: a world made in flight mode (the ten minutes of play), book text in flight mode (α35a), a night of overnight mode in flight mode (α43a), and play with no network call, the APK holding no `INTERNET` permission (α35a's `verify-apk.sh`); and the short list for the owner's judgement (`RES-22`): the pace years to write into `TIM-19` and `CUL-33`, `WLD-04`'s measured value, the thoughts' and kinds of event's counts against "about 100", the scores of the new moments (A10.10), the herds, threshing and hammering on the reel, and whether the whole arc reads as a believable history.
   An independent reviewer checks it (A15.13's process, `PRC-09`); it is published as a private page with the Artifact tool and linked in the note, with a copy at `reports/stage-7.html`, its links opening worlds and entries (`kindling://open`, α11b).
7. `T53b.7` **The release candidate and the stage close (`RES-06`, `RES-22`, `PRE-17`, `PRC-10`, `PRC-11`, A12.7, A15.12).** Run the stage's list (A15.12) and `tools/check.sh --deliver` last, as P0's step 6 runs it; `versionCode=7532`, `versionName=a53b`, the release candidate's APK and web build, and `dist/NOTE.md` with `Update: small`, what is new, what to try, what is rough, the IDs delivered, both links and the stage report's link; then P0's steps 5 to 8; no GitHub release is made and no commit status set.
   The note asks the owner for six things: the `KDB1:` code from a benchmark run, the `KDT1:` code from the writer check (A12.7: at each stage close), ten minutes of play in flight mode with sound on (step 4 below), the reel heard once on the speaker and once on headphones, the signing passphrase if not yet set, and a few lines answering the report's list.
   When the reply comes: decode the codes into `bench/phone/a53b.json` and the trap results, and compare the hashes (a difference keeps the stage open, A15.9); set the director's bars and scores and the reel's levels only as the owner asks, each logged in `data/TUNING-LOG.md` (`PRN-17`); record the review in `reports/stage-7-review.md`; republish the report with the phone's figures; and mark Stage 7 done in the status table (P0: a stage is done when its report is accepted, `RES-06`).

**Data:** `scenes/review-camp-7.toml`, `scenes/review-model-sheet-7.toml`; `bench/budgets.toml` (`MIL-07`'s budget and rows); `data/text/help.md` (the new controls' cards); `assets/LICENSES.md`; `reports/risks.toml`; `reports/principles.toml`; after the reply, `data/tuning/director.md`, `data/tuning/sound.md` and `data/TUNING-LOG.md`.

**Tests:**
- `kd-tools` (`RES-06`): α07e's `report::tests::every_part_present` gains the full test's windows and checks, `MOM-08`'s and `MOM-12`'s results, `WLD-04`'s value and the stage budget of 1; `report::tests::self_contained`.
- `python3 tools/filecheck.py selftest` gains `ids --stage MIL-07` fixtures (an unmapped `MIL-07` feature, a merge without its review line), each failing.
- `kd scene run --stage MIL-07`, `kd kill-test --kills 100`, `kd det` in every form, `kd world check --starts 100` and `filecheck.py ids --stage MIL-07` pass; `sharp-stone` and `sharp-stone-control` pass by `RES-03`; `a45-mom08-heap` and `a47b-mom12-green-pots` pass by `RES-17`.
- `kd-text`'s trap tests pass in the cloud (A12.7), and the phone's `KDT1:` passes.
- Screens: the contact sheet in the cloud (A15.11), no page errors or blank frames, every view in both orientations passing A12.1's layout checks; Web (Playwright): `fresh_install_to_an_open_world_without_help` (`PRE-40`'s Done when); `kd sound render --reel` makes the reel in the cloud with every sound traced (A13.14).

**On the phone:**
1. Install the release candidate over α53a's; unplug the phone, open Settings, long-press the version line, tap Benchmark and leave the phone alone for about 20 minutes; then tap Copy and paste the `KDB1:` code in your reply.
2. Tap Review: scroll the sheet (each stop from the person to the globe at noon and dusk, the model sheet with every launch thing, the three clips), then let the reel play once on the speaker and once with headphones: do the herds, threshing and hammering sound right?
3. Tap Writer check (about 5 minutes, screen on) and paste the `KDT1:` code.
4. First save the Year-500 pace world from the report's link to the phone (if the note gives its `KDW1:` code instead, as α52's T52.9 allows past 50 MB, make it with Make test world on the charger the night before, A15.4); then switch on flight mode and play for about ten minutes with sound on: tap New world and watch it made and settled with no network (`PLT-03`); since a new world takes centuries to reach copper, Make test world `a45 · First fields` and watch a harvest; Make test world `a46a · River village` and tap the village; Make test world `a47b · Green pots` and watch the kiln opened and the first copper noticed; then import the saved Year-500 world (Worlds, Import), or open the one made from its code, and read its book of ages from the first sharp flake to the first copper, age by age (`SCP-16`'s *now possible* for `MIL-07`: the whole arc, from caves to first copper, in a few hundred years, at a watchable speed).
5. Open the report from the note and answer its short list in a few lines.

**Not in this alpha:** layers beyond the launch arc, such as bronze or writing (`VIS-03`, `RSK-05`); fixes the stage review asks for, which come as further alphas the coordinator adds after the review.

**Risks:**
- The owner's reply taking days: the stage closes when the review is recorded (`RES-22`).
- The phone below the stage budget of 1 game year a minute: the report names the costliest systems from the probe and brings them to the owner (`PLT-04`, A16.1), since there is no later stage to win the time back in, never by a cheaper mind (A8.21).
- The full pace test failing a window: α52's options go to the owner in the report (`RES-16`), and the stage closes only with the owner's choice recorded.
- The pace world's export over 50 MB: its `KDW1:` code makes it on the phone instead, overnight on the charger (α43a), and the report says so.
- Phone and cloud hashes differing: the stage stays open until `kd diverge` finds the cause (A15.9, A17.6).
